name: ¡Hablemos Juntos!
description: ¡Hablemos Juntos! is a student-run initiative aimed at equipping Yale health professional students with the linguistic and cultural skills needed to better communicate with Spanish-speaking patients. First started by Yale medical students and piloted with peers in the preclinical phase of training, ¡Hablemos Juntos! offers in-person workshops taught by native Spanish speakers, during which learners discuss clinical cases in Spanish, learn key medical Spanish terminology, and practice communication skills. name: [HIATUS] Contemplatives at Yale Divinity
description: This group is on hiatus. This means no active leaders currently lead the group, membership is locked and no events or activity operates under the group. Should students wish to enquire about reactivating this student organization, they should reach out to osa.yds@yale.edu. Our mission is to hold a contemplative space of prayer and practice for the Yale Divinity School community. We gather to open ourselves to receive and consent to God’s loving presence through the disciplines of the Christian contemplative tradition. name: 2026 BBS Orientation
description: The Yale Combined Program in the Biological and Biomedical Sciences is home to over 700 graduate students across over a dozen departments. This Group facilitates information transfer for first year students to help acclimate them to New Haven and their graduate journey at Yale.

name: 25-26 First Year Counselors
description: First Year Counselors, colloquially known as FroCos are a hallmark of Yale’s advising system. This program provides first-year students access to experienced, mature, and knowledgeable members of the senior class who strive to ease their transition to the academic, social, and cultural life of Yale College. FroCos work with their Residential College Dean and Head of College, along with an array of campus partners to help first-year students define a sense of self, a sense of place, and a sense of responsibility.

name: Abdallah S. Kamel Center for the Study of Islamic Law and Civilization
description: The Abdallah S. Kamel Center for the Study of Islamic Law and Civilization at Yale Law School brings prominent scholars of Islam to the Yale campus for public lectures, seminar discussions, visiting fellowships, and visiting professorships.

name: Addiction Medicine Collaborative
description: The AMC is an interdisciplinary student organization among the Yale health professional schools that seeks to collaboratively enhance professional and public education concerning substance use; to promote and foster the interests of students, health professionals, and advocates for substance use assistance and recovery; and to encourage scholarly inquiry concerning substance use disorders as they impact health care professionals and the public that we seek to serve.

name: Adventist Campus Fellowship
description: Our mission is to inspire Seventh-day Adventist Christian students and faculty members to be disciples of Christ and empower them to share the everlasting gospel on campus.

name: Africa SIG
description: The Africa SIG is a group of engaged students interested in the environmental challenges and opportunities on the continent. The purpose of Africa SIG is two-fold: (1) to serve as a forum for information exchange and research support for members; (2) to create opportunities on campus to engage with the vibrant culture of Africa. The SIG hosts and co-sponsors talks with scholars and practitioners, movie screenings, and cultural experiences to share the colourful traditions that have existed for centuries in Africa.

name: Afro-American Cultural Center
description: Vision: To foster a vibrant community of Black scholar-leaders and others who are committed to preserving and promoting the historical, cultural, intellectual and social movement traditions of the African Diaspora at Yale, in New Haven, and throughout the world. Mission: Established in 1969, the Afro-American Cultural Center ("the House") has a rich history of serving as Yale's home away from home for its Black student body and all campus and local community constituents who wish to learn about and celebrate the cultures and traditions of the African Diaspora. name: AI for Health Equity
parent: Yale School of Public Health Student Organizations
description: The mission of this student group is to enable health practitioners to become designers and not just consumers of artificial intelligence. Through robust lectures, reading circles and working groups, we aim to promote a healthy curiosity about AI and build tangible skills. Facilitated by the co-chairs, the group will be open to all Schools but anchored at the School of Public Health. We aim to bring industry experts such as AI founders, researchers, investors and CPOs to engage with the group.

name: Alexander Hamilton Society: Yale Undergraduate Chapter
description: The Alexander Hamilton Society (AHS) is a non-partisan, not-for-profit, national organization that seeks to identify, educate, and launch young women and men into foreign policy and national security careers imbued with the Hamiltonian perspective of strong and principled American leadership in global affairs. Hamiltonians are united by a deep conviction, rooted in the history of the last century, that the world is a better, safer, and more prosperous place when the United States is willing and able to lead. Engaging citizens from all walks of life and at every stage in their careers, AHS seed

name: Allan Bloom Forum
description: The Allan Bloom Forum is a student organization at Yale University which seeks to promote the public exploration of the ideas which have shaped Western culture through engagement with leading thinkers in the fields of public policy, diplomacy, journalism, and academia. The Forum is named after Allan Bloom, who was a Yale professor, philosopher, and classicist.

name: Allergy, Immunology, Rheumatology Interest Group (AIR)
description: AIR aims to connect students interested in the fields of allergy, immunology, or rheumatology with relevant faculty and clinical/research opportunities. We will cover a range of topics, exploring everything from immune system mechanisms to autoimmune diseases and cutting-edge immunobiologic therapies.

name: Alliance for Dance at Yale College
description: As an umbrella organization we seek to unite the dance groups on campus, bring together the New Haven and Yale dance community and to work for more administrative support for dance on campus. We believe that there should be maximum cooperation within the campus dance community and that as the dance community grows it is important for us to work with the administration to accommodate their needs of rehearsal and performance space. name: Allied Scholars for Animal Protection
description: Allied Scholars for Animal Protection is focused on the abolition of speciesism and exploitation of nonhuman animals. We aim to make students aware of the harms of factory farming and educate about veganism. We also want to provide a space for vegans and animal lovers to build community on campus.

name: Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated, Xi Omicron Chapter
description: The purpose of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated is to cultivate and encourage high scholastic and ethical standards, to promote unity and friendship among college women, to study and help alleviate problems concerning girls and women to improve their social stature, to maintain a progressive interest in college life, and to be of service to all mankind.

name: Alzheimer’s & Aging Public Health Initiative (AAPHI)
parent: Yale School of Public Health Student Organizations
description: The Alzheimer’s & Aging Public Health Initiative (AAPHI) is a student-led organization dedicated to building compassionate, community-centered solutions for Alzheimer’s disease and aging populations. We bring together students, caregivers, patients, and local organizations to advance public health through service, advocacy, research, and education. Our mission is to mobilize students across disciplines to design innovative projects, foster meaningful collaborations, and create a supportive network that uplifts caregivers, empowers communities, and improves the well-being of individuals and fam

name: Alzheimer's Buddies
description: NAB functions by pairing college students with residents in local Alzheimer's/dementia care facilities for weekly one-on-one visits. These students work with both family members and staff to determine the best way to utilize their visits in order to learn more about the interests and lives of the residents, thereby forming connections that help combat the isolation often felt by residents in such facilities. Additionally, NAB chapters in the past have helped educate campus communities about AD, launched music therapy initiatives, and performed clinical research studies. For more information ab

name: American College of Healthcare Executives (ACHE)
description: American College of Healthcare Executives (ACHE) is an international professional society of 40,000 healthcare executives who lead hospitals, healthcare systems and other healthcare organizations. ACHE's mission is to advance our members and healthcare management excellence. Yale ACHE offers networking, education, and career development to students aspiring to pursue healthcare management roles at Yale SPH, SOM, Nursing, Medical School, and the PA program. In the past few years, there has been an average of 100 Yale ACHE chapter members. There will be a variety of ACHE events over the course o

name: American Constitution Society for Law and Policy at Yale Law School
description: The American Constitution Society is the largest student group at Yale Law School. ACS@YLS aims to foster community-wide discussion over progressive issues in American law and provide a forum for all members of the Yale Law progressive community to pursue their interests, educate the wider community, and bring scholars and practitioners together to find the best way to effect progressive change. name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
description: The vision AISES is for the next seven generations of Native scholars and students to advance students and scholars representation in the STEM industries, and bring forth a tacit understanding of how science and indigenous knowledge is intertwined.

name: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics: A Yale Student Branch
description: YAIAA exists to grow and support the Yale aerospace community by making the field accessible to students of all backgrounds. We provide mentorship, hands-on opportunities, and strong industry connections to help students explore careers and build skills. Through a collaborative and inclusive environment, we aim to create meaningful impact for members while supporting Yale College’s mission of academic growth and engagement beyond the classroom.

name: American Medical Student Association
description: We see opportunities to reshape medicine as future physicians. Our vision is a world where health care is accessible, medicine is affordable and systems support the diversity we see around us. We're the next generation of physicians, leaders and change agents. Seventy years strong, with roughly 30,000 active members all across the globe, AMSA is a student-led, national association that exists to cultivate, inspire and inform medical students.

name: American Medical Women's Association at Yale – an Undergraduate Organization
description: The American Medical Women's Association at Yale aims to create a diverse and inclusive community dedicated to health equity and the advancement of women and non-binary undergraduate students in medicine, through education, leadership, and advocacy.

name: American Public Health Association (APHA) - Yale Student Chapter
description: Yale-APHA is the Yale chapter of the American Public Health Association, the oldest, largest, and most diverse organization for public health professionals across the world. The mission of Yale-APHA is to: 1) Foster professional and academic development of Yale School of Public Health students, 2) Develop relationships with undergraduate and graduate students with interests in public health and other allied-health professions and 3) Propagate the mission and goals of the American Public Health Association.

name: American Red Cross at Yale
description: The American Red Cross at Yale seeks to serve as a local community service organization at Yale and in New Haven, providing aid on a more regional scale than its parent organization. We serve as an intermediary between the students and faculty of Yale University and the American Red Cross. We host blood drives on the Yale campus, recruiting Yale graduate and undergraduate students as well as the broader community to donate blood and fulfill the Red Cross's local blood needs.

name: American Sign Language at Yale--An Undergraduate Organization
description: ASLaY seeks to foster a community of diverse ASL signers of all abilities and backgrounds. We aim to provide a space for those interested in sign language to gather and to learn from one another. In addition, we seek to celebrate the beauty and poeticism of sign. ASLaY seeks to fill a gap in the representation of languages on Yale's campus. We try to advocate for more ASL opportunities on campus to further foster and develop a campus-wide appreciation of ASL.

name: American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Student Chapter at Yale
description: To foster a diverse and inclusive community of undergraduate students and faculty dedicated to advancing biochemistry and molecular biology through education, research, and outreach, while providing networking and professional development opportunities.

name: Amoriem Labs: Undergraduate Game Developers
description: We are a group of students interested in game design, programming, character design, graphic design, animation, and music composition, working together to create indie games. We aim to develop creative games, learn about the game development process, and support students interested in working in the gaming industry.

name: Andover Newton

description: The Annand program offers resources that enable all YDS students to discover fundamentals of prayer and creative faith practices for spiritual growth. Seminarians have the opportunity to engage in individual or group spiritual direction with one of the many experienced lay and ordained Annand Program mentors. Mentors represent a variety of theological traditions and denominational backgrounds. Students can participate in facilitated small groups exploring such topics as vocational discernment, contemplative prayer, and faith practices of particular theologians. name: Applied Philosophy in Neuroscience
description: The Applied Philosophy in Neuroscience (APHINE) organization fosters interdisciplinary collaboration between the neuroscience and philosophy departments at Yale University. Through journal club meetings, invited speaker series, and cross-departmental seminars, APHINE provides a platform to critically examine the theoretical frameworks, explanatory limits, and philosophical implications of contemporary neuroscience.

name: Arab Students Association

name: Arnold Air Society
description: To further the purpose, traditions, and concepts of the United States military and aerospace power by aiding in community awareness and to create a more efficient relationship among Air Force officer candidates, both within the Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps and with members of Silver Wings.

name: Asia SIG
description: About Asia, For Asia, Beyond Asia.

name: Asian American Cultural Center (AACC)
description: The Asian American Cultural Center (AACC) plays a key role in ensuring the development and enhancement of Yale University's commitment to the Asian and Asian American community. The AACC seeks to build a dynamic Asian and Asian American presence at Yale, support student exploration of identity development, and empower them to take an active role in shaping their learning experiences. name: Asian American Students Alliance
description: AASA creates a community where students of the Asian diaspora feel empowered to explore their identity, both politically and culturally.

name: Asian Crossroads at Yale - a Student Union
description: Asian Crossroads at Yale (ACY) is a student-led organization that fosters conversations around Central Asia, a region that has long bridged vibrant cultural traditions and modern growth and trade. Accordingly, ACY seeks to raise the profile of economic, social, and political development in the region, while also providing a space for students to engage with Central Asian culture.

name: Asian Graduate & Professional Student Council
description: Asian Graduate Network (AGN) is a student organization whose mission is to build a lasting community amongst Yale graduate and professional students. We strive to do this through professional development opportunities, mentorship, coalition building, and collaboration with organizations both on and off campus. We welcome any community member to attend an event hosted by AGN and support us through our mission.

name: Asian Jewish Union
description: Our members identify as both Asian and Jewish, yet their experiences cannot be fully defined by either culture alone. The mission of the Asian Jewish Union (AJU) is to support and celebrate Asian Jewish students at Yale. We aim to cultivate a welcoming community for Asian Jewish students and contribute to the broader tapestry of Asian Jewish culture.

name: Asian Network at Yale
description: The mission of the Asian Network at Yale is to connect, inspire, and empower the community of Asian Heritage professionals, supporting Yale's ability to excel in an increasingly complex, competitive and diverse world.

name: Asian Pacific American Law Students' Association
description: The Asian Pacific American Law Students' Association (APALSA) serves the interests of its membership by fostering a community within the law school and strengthening ties in the broader Asian Pacific American legal community.

name: Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association
description: We are an organization of Asian American and Pacific Islander American (APIA) medical students committed to addressing the unique health challenges of APIA communities through education, outreach, advocacy, and service, and to providing support, mentorship, and community for APIA students at the Yale School of Medicine.

name: Asian Recipes at Yale - an Undergraduate Organization
description: Asian Recipes at Yale - an Undergraduate Organization (ARAY) aims to share and celebrate Asian flavors and stories within the Yale community and beyond. We want to help connect people who love food and are interested in Asian cuisine by: 1. facilitating conversations and bonding through food events, 2. sharing our recipes with the community, 3. and providing a space for navigating Asian identity through food and food-related arts and media.

description: Asian-ish aims to promote diversity, celebrate multicultural and mixed Asian culture, and create a community for students of mixed Asian descent.

description: Assembly: Undergraduate 3-D Art Collective at Yale exists to provide undergraduates with a welcoming space to explore and develop skills in three-dimensional art forms that blend creative practice with STEM principles, such as woodworking, sewing, metalworking, stained glass, and print-based processes. We serve students of all experience levels by offering shared workspaces, tools, mentorship, and hands-on learning opportunities that emphasize design, material science, engineering thinking, and experimentation. description: ACSSY is an independent, non-political and non-profit organization dedicated to the goal of promoting social, intellectual and cultural activities for Chinese students and scholars at Yale and for other interested members of the Yale community. It will also strive to provide opportunities and benefits for its members by facilitating the exchange of information between China and overseas Chinese students and by protecting the interests of its members on campus as well as in the United States.

name: Asterisk* Journal of Art and Art History
description: The Asterisk* Journal of Art and Art History is concerned with providing an outlet for critical discourse around art for undergraduates, whether it be through practice or theory. Based in New Haven at Yale University, Asterisk* is one of the few peer-reviewed, intercollegiate, bi-annually published art and art history journals at the undergraduate level. We are dedicated to highlighting art historical narratives shedding light on topics that are often left to the margins. name: Athletes in Action
description: At Yale AIA, our vision is to see ourselves, our community and the world deeply changed by the love of Christ. We seek to reach out to students through large group meetings, fun activities, and individual connections. We welcome people of all backgrounds to explore the Christian faith. We meet weekly during the academic year and have Bible studies throughout the week, fellowship activities, and retreats throughout the year.

name: AYUDH
description: AYUDH aims to empower our communities and ourselves through selfless service. We work closely with the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development . The Yale chapter is open to everyone from any stage of life or background and meets to partake in volunteering activities, such as planting trees and serving meals at soup kitchens. We also explore the essence of compassion through discussions, invited speakers, and creative expression. Our initiatives for each year can be found at https://www.ayudh.org/initiatives-1.

name: Ballet Folklórico Mexicano de Yale - Undergraduate Organization
description: Ballet Folklórico Mexicano de Yale was founded in the fall of 1998 by a group of undergraduate students dedicated to the expression of Mexican culture and traditional folk dance. Since its founding, the group has had the privilege of performing at numerous cultural and educational events at Yale, throughout Connecticut, and elsewhere in the Northeast. As the only Mexican folk dance group on campus, Ballet Folklórico does not hold auditions. description: Towards a non-extractive architecture

name: Being Well at Yale: Employee Well-Being
description: To create and sustain a culture, community and environment in which wellness is a core value and measure of excellence at Yale. Building on the existing resources at Yale and guided by the Wellness Leadership Group, Being Well at Yale will engage and support Yale employees in the progression towards healthier lifestyles through: Meaningful partnerships across the Yale community Integrated sources of wellness communication Healthier work environments Accessible programs Outreach and screening Self-assessment and personal health improvement plans Aggregate data gathering and outcome measurement

name: Berkeley College Orchestra
description: The Berkeley College Orchestra is dedicated to the promotion of a musical presence on the Yale campus and the greater Connecticut area. To achieve this goal, the BCO provides a place for students to study and practice the performance of music without grades and seeks to foster a community of musicians with similar goals. To this end, BCO holds weekly rehearsals and three free public concerts during the school year and one educational concert for New Haven public school students.

name: Berkeley Divinity School
description: "The mission of Berkeley Divinity School at Yale is to form and transform lay and ordained leaders for the present and the future Episcopal Church and Anglican Communion. A Christian community of worship, learning, and service, it shares in the ecumenical and scholarly vocations of Yale Divinity School." Berkeley calls its members to become a life-long Christian community of faith, learning, and service, offering all we have for the sake of God and the gospel in transforming the church and the world. description: Welcome. We’re the bioethics interest group (BIG). Ethics is philosophy, and good philosophers always start with a question. So here’s a question for you to ponder. Would you agree with this statement? "I think it’s important to make at least one friend at YSM who strongly disagrees with my most deeply held convictions." If the answer is yes, come hang out with us! If the answer is no, come hang out with us anyway! name: Bioinformatics Support Hub
description: The Bioinformatics Support Hub provides free bioinformatics support and instruction on omics data analysis for various kinds of biomedical research projects. By request, it also provide letters of support for grants and also collaborate on analyzing the data.

name: Birding (SIG)
description: Our mission is to encourage an appreciation for birds and local ecosystems while creating an inclusive community for students interested in birdwatching, conservation, and outdoor observation. It will connect students with nature through accessible, educational, and socially engaging birding events. Most importantly, members don't need any previous experience or interest to be part of our community!

name: Black Church at Yale
description: BCAY—the Black Church at Yale—is a student-run and pastor-guided on-campus church since 1973. We aim to love God fully, love people courageously, and serve others wherever we are—in short, Love God, Love People, and Serve the Nations. We are a Christ-centered, interdenominational fellowship that views God as a loving Father who desires a relationship with His creation. Through intentional relationship-building and practical teachings, we aim to develop Spirit-led leaders who will impact all areas of society after leaving Yale. name: Black Church Studies Certificate Program
description: The Black Church Studies Certificate Program (BCSCP) at Yale Divinity School (YDS) offers a Certificate in Black Church Studies for students who wish to respond to the evolving work of the Black Church and to the critical needs of marginalized communities. The program is open to students interested in serving in historically Black congregations, and /or who are inspired by the rich and ecumenically diverse traditions of the Black Church. name: Black Graduate Student Network at Yale
description: The Black Graduate Network (BGN) at Yale unites all graduate and professional students of African descent, regardless of their school affiliation for fellowship, networking opportunities and service. BGN is open to all members of the Yale Community. BGN also strives to support and supplement the political, social, and community efforts of other schools and departmental minority organizations.

name: Black Pre-Health Students at Yale - an Undergraduate Organization
description: We are a student organization dedicated to inaugurating an empowering, educational, and preparatory environment for students across the African diaspora interested in pursuing a health-related profession. We incorporate the various branches of health and create an atmosphere that encourages critical conversation, community engagement, and a humanistic approach to medicine. Because of the historical oppression of Black populations in healthcare at large, we hope to increase the numbers of prepared Black leaders and healers in health advocacy and clinical settings.

name: Black Student Alliance at Yale
description: The Black Student Alliance at Yale (BSAY) is a multi-cultural organization dedicated to enhancing the lives of Black students at Yale through political action, community action, and social events. Understanding that the world changes for the better through the determined efforts of concerned people, and that we are strongest when we are united, BSAY exists in order to create that unity and foster that change in hopes of furthering the cause of equality. name: Black. et al.
description: “Black. et al.,” is YSE’s first student-led group specifically designed to meet the needs of BIPOC PhD students and postdocs. ‘B.l.a.c.k.’ stands for BIPOC Leadership Alliance for Culture and Knowledge. The“et al.” symbolizes the myriad ways BIPOC students show up at YSE beyond their commitments as students. This organization is founded on the principles of well-being, scholarship, service, fellowship and belonging.

name: BlackGen Capital at Yale – an Undergraduate Organization
description: BlackGen Capital is a 100% minority-owned student investment fund. We close the access gap by creating a pipeline for talented, Black, Hispanic, and Native American students interested in entering the financial services industry.

name: BlackOut
description: To provide community, camaraderie, and support for LGBTQQIAP+ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, questioning, queer, intersex, asexual, pansexual +) individuals of the African Diaspora. We aim to give them the space to engage and wrestle with the intricacies of race, most specifically Blackness, as it relates to the broader queer culture.

parent: Yale Jackson School of Global Affairs

name: Bold in Blue
description: Our mission is to create a vibrant and supportive community for Black students, with a special focus on generational African American students, who share a passion for dance and cultural expression. Through our performances, we aim to celebrate and showcase the richness of Black American culture, blending traditional and modern influences in music, movement, and storytelling. We strive to empower our members by fostering creativity, confidence, and connection while promoting the beauty and resilience of our heritage.

name: Boosted FC
parent: Yale School of Public Health Student Organizations
description: Empowering Health Through Inclusive Soccer: Our mission at the Yale School of Public Health Soccer Team is to unite our diverse community under a shared passion for soccer while promoting inclusivity and fostering health and wellness. Through the universal language of sport, we aim to create a supportive and welcoming environment where all members, regardless of background or skill level, can come together to play, learn, and thrive. name: Brazil Club at Yale - a Student Organization
description: At Yale, we seek to bring together the Brazilian community. We welcome students from Brazil, Brazilian-Americans, the Lusophone Community, and anyone interested in celebrating our culture, history, and identity. By hosting cultural events and preserving lively traditions, such as our weekly dinners, our club offers a space to make friends, have fun, and feel at home. Members of the Brazil Club also recognize the privilege of studying at Yale and carry a strong sense of responsibility to pay it forward to Brazil. name: Bridges ESL
description: Bridges ESL provides free English language lessons to adult learners in the Greater New Haven area. Tutors develop personalized lessons to help meet students' language goals related to employment, education, citizenship, and daily life. Bridges ESL helps people acquire the English skills necessary to confidently navigate family, work, and community life in the U.S.

name: BRINK! A Review of Books
description: BRINK! A Review of Books is a publication intended to re-open up a space on campus for inquisitive readers and writers to think carefully about a wide range of subjects through one of the most incisive modes of engagement there is: the book review. We believe that a book review is a natural conduit for imaginative and rigorous thinking that invites discussion and debate. Originally founded in 2017, the review aims to publish three issues a year of the highest quality of undergraduate writing.

name: Buddhist Life at Yale
description: Buddhist Life at Yale operates under the auspices of the Yale Chaplain’s Office. We are located in the heart of the University on Old Campus. Our community provides the opportunity to learn about Buddhist teachings and practice meditation.

name: Buena Vista Breakfast Club
description: Our organization hopes to build community around our shared loves of fruit and hot beverages and create a space dedicated to starting the day off right. We will exist to help early risers find community in the wee hours of the morning by sojourning for breakfast and creating a warm space for any who needs a pick-me-up before their day of work begins.

name: Building Bridges - Yale University Student Chapter
description: Founded in 2008 at Yale, Building Bridges is an internationally recognized service project aiming to advance educational opportunities for underprivileged high school students in rural China through an annual service trip developed by students of American and Chinese universities.

name: Bulgarian Society
description: The Bulgarian Society serves as a cultural organization for Bulgarian, Bulgarian American students, students from nearby Balkan countries and students interested in Bulgarian language, culture, and politics at Yale. It is committed to foster cultural, political and historical understanding of the Republic of Bulgaria on Yale campus. It serves the Yale College student body by developing programs and providing resources for those who are interested in Bulgaria-related non-profit works, internships and exchange opportunities.

name: Bulldog Cube Club
description: We are a group dedicated to cubing – the art of solving Rubik’s Cubes and other similar puzzles. Our goal is to provide a fun and friendly environment for those interested in cubing to harbor their passion and to teach people who want to learn how to solve a Rubik’s Cube. Absolutely no experience or knowledge is necessary to join!

name: Bulldogs Racing
description: Members of Bulldogs Racing seek to improve their engineering, project management, and business skills through practical application, by designing and constructing vehicles to compete in the Formula SAE series of race car engineering competitions.

name: Cadence of Yale - Undergraduate A Cappella
description: Founded in 2019, Cadence of Yale is Yale's premier competitive a cappella group. A regular participant in the annual International Championship of Collegiate A Cappella (ICCA), the group is dedicated to telling stories through music as well as collaborating with the global a cappella community. Through original arrangements, choreography, and thoughtful music curation, Cadence seeks to unlock music's communicative power with every performance. description: “Cafecitos at YSM” is devoted to sharing the intricacies of Latin America’s cultures with the YSM community through gatherings which immerse participants in Latin customs, beliefs, and perspectives with reverence and substance. These cultural exposures effect a layered approach to immersion, as they include authentic food, drink, and sweets both from local Latin American businesses and homemade by Cafecitos members, sharing of music with deep cultural importance, and talks by speakers with lived experience and expertise in various aspects of Latin culture. Tapping into campus opportunities, resources, and mentorship, we create a powerful leadership experience to support girls of courage, confidence, and character who make the world a better place.

name: Canadian Students at Yale
description: Empowering and uniting Canadian undergraduate students at Yale by fostering a vibrant Canadian community and providing opportunities for personal and academic growth.

Our activities include hosting guest speakers, running workshops, organizing field trips, and providing networking opportunities for students focused on the nexus between energy and the environment. In addition, we work closely alongside faculty to expand the number of energy-focused course offerings at YSE and to bring in experienced industry professionals as guest lecturers.

name: Engineers Without Borders- Yale College Student Chapter
description: The Mission Statement of EWB-Yale Student Chapter is to help carry out the mission of EWB-USA by developing and implementing its own sustainable engineering projects in disadvantaged communities. Other goals include: 1) gaining practical engineering experience 2) find unique engineering solutions for developing nations 3) to create relationships between Yale students and members of developing communities.

name: English Language Program
description: The English Language Program, part of Yale's commitment to internationalization, supports academic communication and the cultural and professional development of the Yale international community. Offering a program centered on assessment of needs, advising, instruction, and consulting, it draws on the expertise of its instructors and staff, as well as a network of English language resources across Yale.

description: EDSY is a student-led organization passionate about GIS, remote sensing, AI, and conservation tech.

name: Environmental Education Collaborative
description: The Environmental Education Collaborative (EECO) is Yale’s first volunteer student organization dedicated to inspiring a generation of environmentally-conscious K-12 students in New Haven. Through a place-based curriculum, EECO builds strong relationships with local students, schools, coalitions, and community organizations. Volunteers teach weekly lessons, lead interactive activities, and collaborate with community leaders to develop sustained environmental education projects that reinforce student learning beyond the classroom.

name: Environmental Leadership and Training Initiative

name: Environmentalists of Color Collective
description: The Environmentalists of Color Collective aims to build community among students of color who share an interest in the Earth, the outdoors, and environmental justice issues. By centering and celebrating the voices of environmentalists of color, we seek to challenge the historical and ongoing marginalization of people of color within environmental movements. name: Eta Sigma Chapter of Lambda Theta Alpha Latin Sorority Incorporated
description: Lambda Theta Alpha Latin Sorority, Incorporated Eta Sigma Chapter at Yale University strives for unity, empowerment, and academic excellence, while promoting cultural awareness and service to our community. We are dedicated to creating an inclusive space for leadership development, sisterhood, and advocacy for underrepresented voices at Yale and beyond. Our mission is to inspire positive change through education, service, and solidarity, guided by the principles of Lambda Theta Alpha.

name: European Studies Council
description: The European Studies Council at the MacMillan Center promotes innovative research on Europe's past and present in the context of regional and global interactions. The Council collaborates with schools and departments throughout Yale to support faculty, students, and visiting scholars by sharing their interdisciplinary expertise on European affairs with the broader public. The Council aims to foster a wider understanding of Europe as both a place and an idea, reflecting the evolving nature of the region and its network of connections throughout the world.

description: The Faculty with Disabilities at Yale Interest Group was established to support and advocate for faculty members at Yale University who identify as having a disability, as well as their allies. This group works to raise awareness of the unique challenges faced by disabled faculty and to promote an academic and professional environment that is fully inclusive and accessible. description: Freshman Outdoor Orientation Trips (FOOT) is an orientation program of backpacking trips for entering Yale freshmen led by two upper class leaders. Students hike along trails to enjoy the views, cook simple meals, and set up tarps under the stars. Freshmen hear about college life first-hand from older students. It is also our goal to help students, staff, and faculty make the connection between the academic and the personal facets of agriculture, by illustrating how and where the food they eat is produced. The group works actively with local farmers and producers, as well as international agricultural and food system issues.

There are more than 800 alumni in the extensive Fox Fellowship network. description: The Graduate Student Assembly is an elected body of Yale students in the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences. The Assembly's goals are to identify the needs and concerns of graduate students, consider possible solutions, and present these to the Dean and other administrators. We also discuss, propose, and advise on possible changes to Graduate School policy proposed by the administration. The assembly provides a means for communication and deliberation both among graduate students and between graduate students and other members of the Yale community.

Participants will be afforded the opportunity to acquire valuable insights into plant propagation techniques and gain comprehensive knowledge about the diverse plant collections housed within the Marsh Botanical Garden.

description: The GSAS Office of Embedded Mental Health and Wellness provides free mental health and wellness programming to all Graduate School of Arts and Sciences students. This includes drop-in therapy appointments with a licensed mental health therapist, GSAS-exclusive group therapy options, and a variety of events and workshops to promote self-care and wellbeing during graduate school. With ever-increasing numbers of international Koreans coming each year, it is important that we provide a community where they feel safe and belonged to smooth major cultural and geographical transitions they may have had to make. We aim to build a home-away-from-home.

description: Harmony Healing is an organization devoted to spreading inspiration and hope through the power of music performance. Our mission is to bring free musical performances, instrument education, and opportunities to perform to underserved neighborhoods across New Haven. We believe music has the unique ability to unite, heal, and uplift individuals and entire communities. description: The Harvey Cushing/John Hay Whitney Medical Library provides access to an extensive array of information resources and tools, offers research assistance and expertise, and delivers meaningful services to our users, to support innovation and excellence in biomedical research, patient care, and the development of scholars and future leaders in healthcare.

description: The HAVEN Free Clinic is a student-run primary care clinic that partners with Yale University to provide the New Haven community access to comprehensive, high-quality health care free of charge. Our model is unique because we include members across various disciplines in health care, including medicine, nursing, physician's associate programs, and public health. name: HAVEN Medical-Legal Partnership
description: The Haven MLP is a partnership with HAVEN, a free clinic operated by Yale medical students every Saturday for uninsured patients, the great majority of whom are also undocumented immigrants. Law student volunteers work onsite at the clinic and meet directly with patients to conduct legal screening and identify issues that should be referred to NHLAA for possible legal representation. Common legal issues include immigration, wage theft, landlord/tenant concerns, and domestic violence. name: Health and Education Advocates for Refugees
description: Our organization's main mission is to provide accessible and comprehensible educational resources and programming on physical and mental health necessities, and give Yale students opportunities to serve refugee populations in New Haven.

name: Health and Environment at Yale (HEY) SIG
description: The HEY SIG provides a critical opportunity to provide a unique, facilitated environment for students to pursue greater understanding of issues relevant to their personal, academic, and professional endeavors in the context of human and environmental health. We wish to provide an opportunity for YSE students to learn and discuss issues at this critical intersection – and, to break out of traditional siloes to explore emerging and pressing issues with each other and with leading experts.

Our goal is to hold open space for conversation, facilitate the sharing of diverse experiences, and discuss our responsibilities as practitioners within the context of war, conflict, and public health. By exploring the central tenets of resistance and liberation, we hope to foster an environment of curiosity and learning around complex and oftentimes overlooked issues.

description: Founded in 2018, Hippo is a student-run literary and arts magazine at Yale University. We accept all kinds of creative writing, from poetry and prose to plays, and art of any medium. name: Hixon Center for Urban Sustainability
description: The Hixon Center bridges scientific knowledge with practical solutions to create vibrant, equitable, and sustainable cities. Our mission is to tackle pressing urban challenges by providing accessible and actionable resources, educating the public, and training future leaders. Through convenings, collaborations, and student fellowships, we support communities and practitioners in shaping sustainable urban environments. Founded in 1998, the Center continues the Hixon family's legacy of advancing urban sustainability locally and globally.

name: Hong Kong Students Association
description: The Hong Kong Students Association (HKSA) is a home away from home for students with ties to Hong Kong. We are a community group for those born and bred in Hong Kong, third culture kids who lived in Hong Kong at a certain point in their lives, individuals whose families emigrated from Hong Kong, and everyone in between. We aim to bring people together through shared cultural experiences, build community, and embrace all the various interpretations of what it means to be a Hong Konger.

name: House of Cards
description: Few students today know how to play classic card games such as Cribbage, Euchre, Gin Rummy, and Pinochle. In order to solve this problem, our organization aims to provide a welcoming environment for people to learn these games and make new friends.

name: Hunger and Homelessness Action Project
description: The Yale Hunger and Homelessness Action Project (YHHAP) is a student organization using education and action to alleviate housing and food insecurity in New Haven. Not-for-profit, we use our direct service, community involvement, and advocacy efforts to address root causes and to support immediate and long-term solutions for local food and housing deprivation.

name: Implementation Science Group
description: The ISG aims to help students with interest in public health and healthcare services to gain a foundation in Implementation Science by exposing them to high quality implementation science research, training, programming/practice, and resources. At ISG, we aim to bridge the gap between knowledge and practice in public health and healthcare.

name: India at Yale - An Undergraduate Organization
description: India at Yale is an undergraduate organization for anyone interested in Indian culture. We aim to bring Yale's Indian community closer by hosting social and cultural events throughout the year. We hope to proliferate interest among the Indian diaspora at Yale by serving as a space for Indians on campus to connect with and share their roots. We are dedicated to enhancing social, academic, and community engagement while celebrating Indian culture.

name: Indigenous Peoples of Oceania
description: The Indigenous Peoples of Oceania at Yale (IPO) is dedicated to providing Oceanic students with the opportunity to build community, advocate for, and celebrate the identities, traditions, and diverse experiences of those Indigenous to Pasifika. IPO strives to uplift Oceanic student voices within the broader Yale community and serve as a platform for Oceanic-centered social events, educational opportunities, and student activism.

name: Indigo: An Undergraduate Arts Organization at Yale
description: Indigo is concerned with providing Yale students with opportunities to engage in the visual arts. This involves, but is not limited to: semesterly art galleries, weekly studio sessions for practicing art hobbyists, art-making events in collaboration with other extracurricular or cultural groups on campus, and engagement activities with New Haven’s art scene. Indigo’s main tenet is that visual arts is an interdisciplinary endeavor: between Yale and New Haven, and between the visual arts and other disciplines.

name: Indonesian Yale Student Association
description: The mission of the Indonesian Yale Students Association (IYA) is to support Indonesian-identifying students and those with an interest in Indonesian culture at Yale University. Partnering with the Yale School of Music and Yale Divinity School, as well as other academic and professional units at Yale, the ISM prepares its students for careers in church music and other sacred music, pastoral ministry, performance, and scholarship. The ISM engages musicians, artists, clergy, and scholars from around the world in rigorous training and collaboration, and offers a full calendar of concerts, lectures, exhibitions, and other events.

We define social innovation as finding a novel solution to a complex social problem that is more effective, efficient, sustainable, or just than existing solutions, disrupts the status quo, and creates value on a societal rather than individual level.

parent: Yale Jackson School of Global Affairs

name: Japanese American Students Union
description: The purpose of the Japanese American Students Union is to provide a forum on campus for political, social, and cultural conversation for Yale students of Japanese descent and students interested in Japanese culture. To this end, JASU will conduct outreach to the aforementioned students, organize events, and voice the concerns of the Japanese American community to the larger Asian American and University student-body.

name: Japanese Association of Students and Scholars at Yale
description: The purpose of Japanese Association for Students and Scholars at Yale (JASY) is to connect all Japanese and Japan-affiliated people on campus. Our group consists of people from academia, government, industry, or non-profit organizations, providing an opportunity to a network with different backgrounds. This group is open to all interested students and scholars.

name: Jewish Christian Bible Study
description: Jewish Christian Bible Study is dedicated to fostering interreligious dialogue through Biblical study. We seek to learn from one another and our diverse approaches to a shared text, and hope to build a strong, collaborative relationship between Jewish and Christian communities on campus.

name: Jewish Graduate Network At Yale
description: The Jewish Graduate Network works to connect Jewish graduate students from across all the Graduate and Professional Schools. We share resources, connect people to each other, and create opportunities for people to be in community together.

name: Jewish Medical Student Association (Maimonides Society)
description: Welcome to the Maimonides Society, which is a Jewish Medical Student Association for the Yale School of Medicine. The Maimonides Society aims to welcome and support students by creating a Jewish community and family. Over the course of the year, we hold classes, events, dinners, holiday parties, and philanthropic events. The Maimonides Society supports our members by helping in any way we can including connecting students to clergy, learning opportunities, services, etc on the Yale campus. The Maimonides Society continues to evolve and pursue the current students' passions from medical ethics

name: Jewish Students' Association
description: In pursuit of lively and meaningful discourse, the Solomon House is a revival of the centuries-old Yale tradition of the Debate Society. We host events inspired by Talmudic debate, fostering rigorous examination of ideas and perspectives, and encouraging the questioning of everything.

parent: Yale Jackson School of Global Affairs

name: Journal of Literary Translation
description: The Journal of Literary Translation (JoLT) publishes English translations of poetry and prose, literary essays, and pieces on the theory and practice of translation. A bi-annual magazine, JoLT seeks to showcase the excellent work of writers and translators at Yale, to think critically about literary comparison and translation in a variety of contexts, and to explore metaphors for translation through the design of each issue. We also host speaker events, readings, and workshops to promote comparative literature and literary translation in the greater community at Yale.

name: Joyous String Ensemble
description: The Joyous String Ensemble at Yale is dedicated to inspiring audiences and students through the power of music by redefining the possibilities of string and classical instrument performance. As a group at Yale, it would enrich the university’s cultural life by offering performances celebrating diversity and connecting communities through music. The ensemble encourages creative collaboration among students, bridging different backgrounds and perspectives while aligning with Yale’s commitment to leadership, innovation, and cultural exchange.

name: Jumpin’ at Yale — an Undergraduate Double Dutch team
description: Our mission is to promote creative expression through Double Dutch performance that integrates jump rope, dance, and acrobatic skills. We hope to foster a community for students interested in Double Dutch while celebrating the historical significance of the activity in Black and African American culture.

name: Just Add Water
description: Just Add Water, affectionately known as JAW, aims to provide the magic of musical improv comedy to the Yale Community and beyond during our on-campus shows, off-campus gigs, and semiannual tours around the United States. What's more, JAW provides an environment for Yale students to explore themselves and the world around them via improv. These tools have proven invaluable for our members, current and of legend, and explain in part why JAW is considered a second family by its members.

name: Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Sustainability Initiative (JEDSI)
description: The Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Sustainability Initiative (JEDSI) seeks to examine the relationship between social inequalities, lived experiences, and environmental outcomes. To this end, JEDSI currently focuses on eight primary areas of research, teaching, and practice: Environmental History Nature, Outdoor Experiences, Attitudes, and Perceptions Environmental Inequalities, Resilience, and Sustainability Food and Farming: Access, Sovereignty, Food Justice Institutional Diversity, Transparency, and Workforce Dynamics Diversity Pathway Programming New Horizons in Conservation Conference Me

name: K-Pop Dance Society at Yale - YSM Chapter
description: KDSY is a K-pop dance society at Yale, now with a new chapter at YSM. We hope to allow students of all cultural and dance backgrounds to participate in bringing the variety, skill, and vibrancy of Korean dance to the stage. We aim to encourage interaction and collaboration with other dance groups on campus and make KDSY-YSM a reflection of Yale's diverse and creative environment.

name: Kale Skies - art club
description: Kale Skies is a recreational art club dedicated to building a welcoming space where people can connect through creativity. From painting and pumpkin carving to woodworking and beyond, we gather to make art, enjoy music and snacks, and most importantly spend time in good company. Founded as a painting club within the track team, Kale Skies is now open to anyone who wants to participate.

name: Kasama: The Filipino Club at Yale - An Undergraduate Organization
description: Our purpose is to engage the Yale community in issues regarding Filipino culture. We achieve this goal by hosting events that raise awareness of Filipino identity, such as cooking events, group dinners, mixers, cultural shows, and political discussions. Kasama is a small club and our name - translated from Tagalog as "together" - embodies our mission to bring together members of the community both Filipino and non-Filipino. Thus Kasama is involved in the Asian American Cultural Center at Yale, The Asian American Students Alliance, and other umbrella organizations in order to embrace both Filip

name: Kern National Network for Flourishing in Health
description: The Kern National Network for Flourishing in Health (KNN) is a national movement focused on integrating character, caring, practical wisdom and flourishing across the health ecosystem. Its goals are to transform medical and health professions education using the concepts of character, caring, and practical wisdom, to work with healthcare organizations to influence cultures and environments, and to share knowledge and engage partners toward broader policy and systems change. A YSM specific chapter would facilitate a transformation of flourishing among our student body. In practical terms, we wo

name: Korean American Students at Yale
description: The Korean American Students at Yale (KASY) was established in 1984 by a group of students who wanted to promote the cultural, political, and social interests of the community of Korean Americans at Yale. In the thirty-plus years since its inception, KASY has grown both in size and influence, but still remains dedicated to its founding principles. Known as a vibrant and thriving undergraduate organization, KASY functions as a promoter of cultural awareness, a vehicle for political action, and most importantly, a tightly-knit family.

name: Korean Graduate Student Association at Yale
description: Korean Graduate Student Association at Yale is an active organization on campus with around 150-200 members. Our purpose is to help Korean and Korea-interested graduate students navigate opportunities and communities around campus. The purpose of the organization is to enhance the network and the academic and vocational cooperation among the Korean graduate students at Yale, and to provide social, cultural and educational functions for Korean graduate students as well as the general student body at Yale. We also serve as as a liaison among Korean Associations in the New England region and we s

name: Kpop Dance Society at Yale - a graduate student organization
description: K-pop Dance Society at Yale (KDSY) is a graduate student organization that hopes to allow students of all cultural and dance backgrounds to participate in bringing the variety, skill, and vibrancy of Korean dance to the stage. We aim to encourage interaction and collaboration with other dance groups on campus and make KDSY a reflection of Yale's diverse and creative environment.

name: La Casa Cultural Julia de Burgos: The Latino Cultural Center at Yale
description: Building on a strong campus community, the Latino Cultural Center promotes a sense of unity among Latinx people at Yale. We are committed to providing a comfortable space where our diverse cultural heritage, history and traditions can be celebrated and explored by all Yale University and New Haven community members. In partnership with our resident organizations, La Casa provides opportunities that foster a sense of belonging and pride while supporting the intellectual, personal, leadership and social development of our students.

name: La Comunidad
description: La Comunidad, the YDS Latine/x Student Group, is dedicated to creating spaces for Latine voices and bodies at YDS to gather and build community of solidarity and support. La Comunidad also seeks to provide resources to promote theological and cultural education for the entire YDS student body preparing for service to the church and the world. La Comunidad hopes to foster comunidad Latina: an open, welcoming place to learn, struggle, and celebrate.

name: La Sociedad of Latine Law Students
description: The La Sociedad of Latine Law Students (LaSo) supports Latinx students at YLS primarily by community building, providing professional and academic mentorship, offering opportunities for political engagement on issues confronting the Latinx community, and connecting members with Latinx alumni and practitioners.

name: La Unidad Latina, Lambda Upsilon Lambda Fraternity, Inc.
description: La Unidad Latina, Lambda Upsilon Lambda Fraternity, Incorporated primarily seeks to take a leadership role in meeting the needs of the Latino community through academic achievement, cultural awareness, community service and promotion of the Latino culture and people. Since its inception in 1982, La Unidad Latina has remained on the vanguard of political and community empowerment by developing influential leaders that strive to exert knowledge and power into its peers in order to attain mutual success. We commit ourselves to academic excellence, leadership development and cultural enlightenment

name: Latin America (LA) SIG
description: The Latin American SIG seeks to create a vibrant and inclusive community for students interested in the region’s economic, social, political, and environmental challenges and opportunities. The SIG serves as a platform to foster academic dialogue, professional development, networking, and cultural exchange while promoting meaningful engagement with Latin America.

name: Latina Women at Yale
description: Latina Women at Yale (LWAY) was founded in 2016 with the mission of fostering a strong and inclusive community for Latina women across all intersectionalities on campus. Today, with over 120 active members, we aim to create opportunities for members to connect, share their experiences, and celebrate the richness of their diverse backgrounds and identities. Through taco nights, mixers, fundraisers, study breaks, and a range of other social, cultural, and professional events, we strive to empower Latina women and cultivate meaningful relationships at Yale and beyond.

name: Latter-day Saint Student Association
description: The Latter-day Saint Student Association (LDSSA) is open to all Yale students with the opportunity to come together in a supportive environment and seeks to educate and raise awareness about the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in the Yale and New Haven communities. Our purpose is grounded in learning, understanding, and relying on the teachings and Atonement of Jesus Christ.

Light and Truth
description: PROMOTING VIEWPOINTS ON YALE'S CAMPUS, LIGHT & TRUTH IS AN ONLINE STUDENT PUBLICATION THAT PROVIDES THOUGHTFUL AND RIGOROUS ESSAYS, ARTICLES, AND OTHER WORKS IN PHILOSOPHY, POLITICS, AND CULTURE.

name: LINK New Haven
description: Link New Haven seeks to close the information gap between community resource providers and disadvantaged residents. The organization operates a free and accessible public resource desk weekly at the New Haven Green staffed by dedicated student volunteers and compiles social service resource guides.

name: Living Water at Yale – an Undergraduate Organization
description: Living Water is Yale's first Christian a cappella group. Founded in 1979, Living Water at Yale exists to spread the Gospel, the good news of God's love and desire for relationship with all of humankind fulfilled through Jesus Christ. As a group, we spread the Gospel by sharing our testimonies of God's faithfulness, singing music that tells His story, glorifying Him through our craft, and reflecting His love and truth in our service toward Yale, New Haven, our respective home communities, and each other.

name: Low Strung
description: Low Strung provides cellists with the opportunity to explore new kinds of cello playing and perform for audiences on campus and worldwide.

name: LuMin at Yale

name: Lutheran Student Organization
description: Through worship, retreats, prayer, and informal gatherings, the Lutheran Student Organization (LSO) provides fellowship for all YDS students involved in Lutheran traditions and beyond. Functioning within YDS's Lutheran Studies Program, students plan Tuesday evening Vespers at Bethesda Lutheran Church and intermittently assist with Lutheran chapel services in Marquand. The LSO also sponsors guest speakers and discussion forums for issues pertinent to the YDS community.

name: M.E.D. Working Group
description: The M.E.D. Working Group is a student-led platform for research and resource-sharing on spatial justice, planetary activisms, and their variegations across visual and material cultures.

description: Magevet's mission is to bring a diverse range of Jewish, Hebrew, and Israeli music to communities around the world.

name: Mahjong Undergraduate Society for Students at Yale
description: The Mahjong Undergraduate Society for Students at Yale will introduce mahjong to the greater Yale community. We will accomplish this goal by providing meeting spaces, mahjong equipment, and experienced players to both novices and veterans of the game throughout the semester. Further, we aim to enrich the cultural experiences of Yalies, current and future by sharing the customs and traditions that have surrounded mahjong.

name: Maison at Yale: An Undergraduate Organization
description: MAISON is a fashion and art collective that aims to spearhead creative expression at Yale through outlets including fashion shows, photoshoots, speaker events, and more. We provide a platform where student creatives can showcase their work and connect with one another, other local creatives, and beyond. Our focus is to be a space where all fashion enthusiasts and artists, regardless of experience, can fulfill their artistic vision.

name: Malaysian and Singaporean Association
description: The Malaysian and Singaporean Association (MASA) supports the interests of Malaysian and Singaporean students, and promotes the culture of both countries at Yale.

name: Mariachi Lux Et Veritas de Yale - A Student Organization
description: Mariachi Luz y Verdad de Yale is the premier Mariachi group at Yale. Through our music, we celebrate Mexican culture and provide an introduction to traditional Mexican music for the greater campus community. We beautify our campus with Mexican folklore music and entertainment. We aim to showcase performances that bring awareness, love, culture, and representation to the Mexican and Latine communities on campus. It serves all students by contributing to the diverse Yale campus and providing the means for cultural appreciation.

name: Marquand Chapel
description: Marquand Chapel is at the heart of Yale Divinity School. Worship is planned and led by students, faculty, and staff of both Yale Divinity School and the Institute of Sacred Music, under the leadership of the Dean of Chapel and a team of staff and students. Worship in Marquand often draws on a wide variety of inherited Christian traditions, with the worship of many denominations being represented. Beyond that, though, we also pay attention to the rising number of people in Western society who have a lively interest in spirituality but feel no connection to traditional forms of church and worshi

name: Marshall-Brennan Constitutional Literacy Project
description: The Marshall-Brennan Constitutional Literacy Project is a national civics education program that sends law students into public high schools to teach courses in constitutional law and oral advocacy. These courses focus primarily on educating high schoolers about their constitutional rights.

name: MATHCOUNTS Outreach: a Yale Undergraduate Organization
description: (1) Build a lasting interest in mathematics and problem solving among middle school students in the New Haven area through weekly tutoring sessions. (2) Support middle school students in their mathematical educations through review and enrichment of material. (3) Create a platform for students to apply their skills through annual competitions and events. (4) Serve the New Haven community by improving the general quality of mathematics education.

name: Matriculate Chapter at Yale - An Undergraduate Organization
description: Matriculate's mission is to empower high-achieving, low-moderate income high school students to make the leap to colleges and universities of best fit with support and advising from undergraduates at Yale.

name: MB&B's Committee of Climate and Diversity
description: Our mission is to promote diversity, equity and inclusion in the department of Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry. We are dedicated to creating an inclusive environment where all members, regardless of their background, feel valued, respected, and empowered to contribute their best. We want to strengthen the sense of community, mutual understanding and belonging through shared activities and social events dedicated to DEI topics.

name: MDiv Cohort Group
description: Space for MDiv current students. Receive news and updates from your year group reps, schedule events together as a program community and connect with other MDiv'ers!

name: Mecha de Yale -- a Yale Student Organization
description: Mecha de Yale is a movement committed to achieving meaningful change through collective action. It is powered by individuals united in challenging the status quo and striving to build respect and equality within an environment too often marked by ignorance. The strength to lead comes from the creative consciousness of its members—los estudiantes—motivated not by self-interest, but by the conviction that, united as one, they can advance the interests of the broader Latine community. Guided by their histories and driven by the hope of a better tomorrow, Mecha de Yale members honor their founding

description: Med Out the Vote (MOtV) is a voter registration/mobilization campaign initiative by AMSA. We are a non-partisan campaign that is dedicated to increasing the civic engagement of healthcare professionals.

description: The Medical Mandarin Interest Group (MMIG) is dedicated to helping students develop their Mandarin skills in an effort to provide the best possible care to an increasingly diverse patient population.

Medical Students for a Sustainable Future at Yale
description: The Medical Students for a Sustainable Future (MS4SF) Yale School of Medicine Student Chapter aims to promote human health in Connecticut and the New Haven community by addressing pollution and climate change through education, service and advocacy.

name: Medicine and Religion Interest Group
description: The Medicine and Religion Interest Group fosters dialogue about the interplay between religion and medicine among students and faculty at Yale University and beyond. We collaborate across departments and schools in the research of religion and medicine and translate and disseminate the fruits of research in order to foster mutual understanding and improve patient care.

name: Medieval Literature Exploration Club
description: MLEC strives to provide an opportunity for Yale students passionate about medieval cultures to explore Yale's vast medieval studies and cultural resources. Too often, medieval studies focus on Medieval Europe, and we hope to actively engage with other cultures and learn about their practices. Engagement includes group discussions, visits to archives and museums, and occasional medieval-themed events to introduce more Yalie's to the field.

name: MEDLIFE at Yale - an Undergraduate Organization
description: MEDLIFE Yale is committed to empowering students to engage in sustainable global health initiatives through service, education, and advocacy. Through partnerships with underserved communities both locally and abroad, our chapter strives to address barriers to healthcare access while promoting long term community development and ethical engagement. By fostering leadership, cultural humility, and interdisciplinary collaboration, MEDLIFE Yale aims to inspire students to become compassionate advocates for health equity and social justice.

name: Mellon Mays & Edward A. Bouchet Fellowship Programs
description: Mellon Mays and Edward A. Bouchet Undergraduate Fellowship Programs reflect an effort to increase the pool of young people qualified to meet the needs of educational institutions into the next century.

Methodist Studies
description: This is a space for YDS students, alumni, and colleagues who share in the Methodist tradition in its many diverse manifestations such as AME, Korean Methodists, and United Methodists. We welcome all who identify with the Wesleyan heritage as well as new seekers searching for a circle of friends in faith. We provide a forum for mutual upbuilding, spiritual formation, doctrinal and polity concerns, and contact with local Methodist clergy. We meet for fellowship, worship, guest speakers, community service, and other activities.

name: Middle Eastern and North African (MENA) Cultural Community
description: The Middle Eastern and North African Cultural Community (MENACC) is an institutional resource that aims to provide holistic support to MENA-identifying students at Yale that encourages their development as well as educates the broader Yale and Greater New Haven communities of their distinct cultures, histories, religions, and needs. This is done through advocacy efforts, educational programming, student organization support, and collaborations with campus partners through an intersectional lens. Established in 2024, this is the first of its kind in the Ivy League.

name: Middle Eastern and North African Law Students' Association
description: The Middle Eastern and North African Law Students' Association provides a forum for engaging the Yale Law School community on the legal, political, social and cultural realities of the peoples of North Africa and the Middle East.

name: Middle Eastern and North African Medical Society
Migration Alliance at Yale - An Undergraduate Organization
description: MAY is a coalition of undergraduate students passionately devoted to aiding refugees, immigrants, and all other migrants in Greater New Haven – through advocacy and direct service.

name: Mission: BRAIN at Yale
description: The Mission: BRAIN Yale Chapter is committed to advancing neurosurgical equity through education, local outreach, and global partnership. We bring together students across disciplines to learn from frontline providers, support underserved communities, and contribute to sustainable, collaborative solutions in global neurosurgery.

name: Mixed Company
description: Mixed Company is an undergraduate organization formed primarily to promote public appreciation of group harmony singing and to educate students at Yale and other educational institutions and the general public about such music.

MonstRAASity

name: Morris Tyler Moot Court of Appeals
description: The Morris Tyler Moot Court competition takes place each year at Yale Law School, culminating in the Harlan Fiske Stone/Thurman Arnold Prize Finals in the spring. All second- and third-year law students are eligible and encouraged to participate.

name: MOVEMENT
description: Yale Movement is a dance and performing arts organization that focuses on Korean pop and open style choreography. We provide a fun, supportive, and constructive outlet to Yale students and the greater New Haven community. We hope to learn and grow together as a team through our creative interests.

name: Movie and Cinema SIG
description: Building community by organizing and promoting movie screenings and cinema trips. The SIG aims to foster discussion about film, lower the financial barrier to enjoy movies, and connect cinephiles to events by sharing announcements about everything related to movies at Yale and beyond.

name: Muslim Law Students' Association
description: The Muslim Law Students' Association serves as a vehicle for gathering Muslims and others interested in learning about Islamic legal issues and issues of concern to Muslims and other minorities.

name: National Lawyers Guild
description: The National Lawyers Guild (NLG) is dedicated to the need for basic change in the structure of our political and economic system.

name: National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers (NOBCChE)-Yale
parent: Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GSAS) Student Organizations
description: The mission of NOBCChE includes building an eminent community of scientists and engineers by increasing the number of underrepresented minorities in the fields of chemistry, chemical engineering, and related disciplines. NOBCChE-Yale and its partners will use a combination of in-person and virtual meetings, workshops, demonstrations, awards, and other events to deliver programming that advances the shared objectives of NOBCChE-Yale and the national organization.

name: National Society of Black Engineers
description: The National Society of Black Engineers, as a national student and professional based organization, does hereby dedicate itself to the development of intensive programs for increasing African-American and other ethnic minority participation in the field of engineering and engineering technology. These programs will be initiated both within and outside the campus community and will serve to strengthen relations between professional industry and the African-American community.
