name: Native American Cultural Center
description: The NACC strives to maintain a permanent and prominent Indigenous presence at Yale that incorporates and supports the success of future Native leaders through recruitment, encouragement, mentoring, service, and the fostering of a community that makes Yale the most sought after Ivy Institution for Indigenous achievement, research and solidarity.

name: Native and Indigenous Student Association at Yale
description: The Native and Indigenous Student Association at Yale (NISAY) [formerly known as ANAAY until 2021] is a student-run political and cultural organization that empowers Indigenous students and advocates for causes throughout Indigenous communities in the global context. NISAY is devoted to the establishment of a Native presence on Campus. The group works towards Indigenous cultural awareness of the Yale Community with a Native perspective through panels, speaker programs, and other events throughout the year.

name: Natyamandala
description: NATYA MANDALA is an Indian classical dance awareness group that promotes traditional Indian dance forms through performance, shows, workshop and other events.

name: Navarasa
description: The mission of Navarasa is to cultivate a vibrant and inclusive community at Yale University where graduate and professional school students can express their passion for dance, particularly through Indian classical dance forms. We aim to foster cultural appreciation, artistic growth, and meaningful connections among members, while promoting diversity and creativity through performances and collaborative events.

name: Nepali Students Society at Yale
description: NSS is an organization for Yale students of Nepali descent, and students that aim to educate and promote Nepal and Nepali culture. This organization provides a forum on campus for political, social, and cultural conversations. Through numerous events and strong community communication, we hope to create positive connections between students of Nepali origin and the local communities around and at Yale.

name: Neuro Divinity: A Student Organization
description: Our objective is to bring together YDS students who identify as neurodivergent in order to processing some of the experiences we often share and affirm each other in our authentic selves in a way that attempts to counteract expectations to hide or masks parts of ourselves and the ways that our brains might work. We will also explore methods of advocacy for people with varied neurological needs or unique perspectives, to support radically authentic self-expression. Our vision is to deepen radical inclusion within YDS as a whole, to embrace neuroinclusion as a valuable component.

name: New Directions in Environmental Law Conference
New Haven Exchange
description: The Yale–New Haven relationship requires a coordinated, student-led movement. Bridging this divide requires students to step beyond the campus bubble and seek genuine connection. These connections must go beyond traditional models of service. Students should build friendships, explore New Haven’s neighborhoods, engage in dialogue with local leaders, and learn from lifelong residents and advocates. The New Haven Exchange propels students to reimagine their role in the city—aiming to foster a cultural shift in how Yalies understand, inhabit, and contribute to their four-year home.

name: New Haven Resource for Essay and Application College Help
description: New Haven REACH is a student-run organization that seeks to provide the information and support necessary for New Haven youth to access the higher education best suited to their dreams, potential, and ambitions. REACH was founded by graduates of the Wilbur Cross Class of 2011, and we now have Yale student volunteers who hail from all over America and all over the world. We all share the core belief that no one should be shut out from attending college just because they don't have the information and support they need to apply.

name: New Haven Urban Debate League
description: Our mission is to empower New Haven's students with the public speaking and critical thinking skills necessary to lead the future.

name: Nurturing Every Sacred Thread (NEST)
description: Nurturing Everyone's Spirituality Together ("NEST") gives voice to community members that are non-Christian, Christian adjacent, Christian pluralist, of diasporic traditions, and spiritual seekers. Yale Divinity School’s mission affirms that “Traditionally and primarily Christian in character, the school welcomes persons of *all faiths* and those of *no faith*.” In this spirit, NEST extends hospitality, love, advocacy, and community to people across the spectrum of belief and non-belief. name: Office for Graduate Student Engagement and Development (OGSED), GSAS
description: The Office for Graduate Student Engagement and Development (OGSED) is committed to building and maintaining a nurturing and caring community of scholars where students from diverse backgrounds and experiences are supported in their professional and intellectual goals and pursuits.

To build our individual and collective skills, all members of the Yale community have an annual sexual misconduct training requirement.

name: Office of Graduate Fellowships
description: The Graduate School's Office of Graduate Fellowships (OGF) seeks to support Yale graduate students when it comes to identifying and successfully applying for external funding opportunities. Join this group to stay up to date on latest news regarding funding opportunities, deadlines and advice with the application process. We also send out monthly newsletters with latest news about funding opportunities and advice for applications. Missed a newsletter? Go to the "Newsletters" tab to see our archive. You can also view up to date general information on external fellowships at: https://gsas.yale.e

name: Office of International Students & Scholars
description: Over 6000 international students and scholars from more than 120 countries call Yale University their home away from home. You come from Albania and Zimbabwe and many places in between and you are making untold contributions to this university. The OISS is here to help and support you throughout your Yale experience and beyond, be it a question about your immigration status or your transition to this new culture and community. We look forward to getting to know you!

name: Office of Nursing Impact
description: The Office of Nursing Impact (ONI) at Yale School of Nursing is committed to transforming the impact of nursing education through community-centered approaches to leadership. Through strategic engagement, education, and world-class simulation design, ONI empowers students, faculty, and staff with the knowledge, skills, and tools to address social and structural factors influencing health, reduce gaps in care, and foster environments that reflect and respond to the communities we serve. Our rigorous interrogation of the arguments of members and philosophers alike will shape stronger philosophical understandings. In turn, these understandings will help students cope with existential dread and help them become better leaders with stronger communication and deduction skills.

name: Open Labs at Yale - a Graduate Student Organization
description: Open Labs organizes science outreach events for K-12 students in the New Haven area. We coordinate multiple forms of outreach including hands-on science demonstrations, science talks, and digital content. All student are welcome to volunteer and collaborate with us!

name: Opera Theatre of Yale College
description: The Opera Theatre of Yale College (OTYC) is the undergraduate opera company at Yale University. Our organization is entirely student-run; every show offers our members the opportunity to learn firsthand the mechanics of performing and producing an opera. Our members are singers, instrumentalists, conductors, theatre technicians, costume and set designers, choreographers, and dancers. OTYC is an immersive extracurricular experience that prepares young artists and administrators for professional life after Yale. By harnessing the passion and enthusiasm of Yale students, we hope to inspire middle- and high-schoolers to seek out further learning and see education as a fun, inviting process. We want to empower students by giving them full choice regarding their Splash day.

The society was founded when the nation's oldest honor society, Phi Beta Kappa, sought to restrict its membership to students in the liberal arts. Our stage is a space for community, empowerment, and the continual celebration of our cultural tapestry.

BSC is the largest undergraduate conference held at Yale University and it continues to grow each year! Our dialogues are designed to build relationships and to spur collaborative action on the highest priority issues facing the world's forests.

Our mission is to sing wonderful music together, become better musicians through vocal performance and rehearsal, to share our music to Yale's campus and audiences across the world, and, most of all, to cultivate meaningful friendships that last a lifetime. Since 1986, the Herald has aimed to provide in-depth, analytical reporting and includes personal essays, interviews and profiles, culture articles, creative writing, reviews, humor, and feature coverage of campus and local happenings. description: UHOPE Haven envisions a future world where New Haven community members and families experiencing homelessness, some of the most vulnerable among us, can freely access dignified and compassionate social services without fear of stigma or judgment. description: UHOPE Haven is a student organization focused on addressing issues prevalent in the unhoused community, primarily focused on health and hygiene. name: Unitarian Universalist Student Group

description: United in Christ's Walk (UCW) is a student-led, InterVaristy-resourced student ministry. It is our mission to know Christ and make Him known. We aspire to live life together as a family, loving each other in grace and truth, reading and studying the Bible, praising and praying, engaging in felloship, and experiencing the transforming power of the gospel.

description: The mission of United Students for Veterans' Health (USVH) is to aid in caring for and enriching the lives of veterans all across the nation. Our most cherished goal is fostering friendships between patients and students. In these relationships, our volunteers give back to those who gave so much. We strive to create a world in which students actively engage with and learn from the significant life experiences of veterans and veterans benefit from the joy and enthusiasm of student volunteers.

name: UNITY

UNITY is best known for its performance of samulnori, a form of percussion music rooted in native Korean religious and cultural practices. name: Universities Allied for Essential Medicines at Yale - a student organization

description: The University Church in Yale is a student-focused church welcoming Christian students of all backgrounds, as well as staff, faculty, post-docs, parents, alumnus/a, parents, and our New Haven neighbors. Our church life is centered around Sunday worship in Yale's historic Battell Chapel, which features beautiful music, thoughtful preaching, and the prayer of a diverse, faithful community. Historically, only a small fraction of science degrees were awarded to women, but in recent decades, women's overall participation STEM fields has steadily increased. description: The Yale Animated Media Student Organization (YAMSO) is a student-led organization dedicated to fostering critical appreciation and thoughtful discussion of animated media as a significant artistic, cultural, and political form. YAMSO serves Yale students interested in engaging with animation from diverse cultures, genres, and traditions. name: Yale Buddhist Student Community
description: Buddhist inquiry, meditation, and spiritual friendship for beginners, seekers, friends from other faiths, and Buddhists of all lineages.

name: Yale Business and the Environment Conference
description: To bridge business and environmental communities at Yale and beyond, creating a platform for learning, dialogue, and connection around sustainable business practices that balance growth with planetary stewardship.

name: Yale Cancer Biology Training Program
description: The Yale Cancer Biology Training Program provides a unique cancer-focused training experience intended to develop the next generation of cancer scientific leaders. Training covers the genetic and biological underpinnings of cancer, the pathway to development of new therapies based upon this knowledge, and the practical challenges in applying these new therapies in cancer clinics.

name: Yale Cancer Center - Cancer Prevention & Control
Yale Cancer Center - Community Outreach and Engagement
Yale Cancer Student Interest Group
description: The Cancer Student Interest Group (CSIG) works closely with the Yale Cancer Center to expose students to oncology and the oncological subspecialties. We coordinate events that seek to connect students with ongoing research, faculty mentors, and shadowing opportunities.

name: Yale Car Club — A Student-Run Organization
description: YCAR is Yale’s premier automotive community for enthusiasts of all kinds. Our mission is to bring together students, alumni, and industry leaders who share a passion for the art, design, and engineering of automobiles, motorcycles, and all things mechanical. Whether you’re a tinkerer, engineer, designer, or simply someone who loves cars, YCAR offers a collaborative space with opportunities to learn, network, and celebrate automobiles through on and off campus events such as car shows, cars & coffee meetups, and automotive media productions.

name: Yale Caribbean Students' Organization
description: The Yale Caribbean Students' Organization (CSO) aims to create a space on Yale's campus for the celebration of the rich and diverse cultures of the Caribbean region and its many diasporas.

name: Yale Center for Asylum Medicine
description: The Yale Center for Asylum Medicine conducts forensic medical interviews and evaluations for asylum-seekers referred to Yale by regional legal groups and community organizations.

name: Yale Center for Business and the Environment
description: To educate and inspire interdisciplinary leaders through business solutions to systemic environmental problems.

name: Yale Center for Environmental Law and Policy
Yale Center for Faith and Culture
description: We seek a world in which everyone can take hold of a life worthy of our humanity. Our purpose is to help people envision and pursue lives worthy of our humanity, through discerning, articulating, and commending visions of flourishing in light of the life and teaching of Jesus Christ and fostering truth-seeking conversations among the contending visions in our world today.

name: Yale Center for Geospatial Solutions
description: Our mission is to create geospatial knowledge that solves humanity’s most pressing challenges.

name: Yale Center for Natural Carbon Capture
Yale Center on Climate Change and Health
description: Climate change represents the greatest public health challenge of the 21st century, and has profound implications for human health, today and in the future. To this end, the Yale Center on Climate Change and Health (CCCH) utilizes research, education, public health practice, and service to help achieve a world with a stable and safe climate; one in which the public's health and diverse ecosystems can thrive. The YSPH Concentration in Climate Change and Health will work to address the severe shortage of public health professionals with the educational background needed to address climate change

name: Yale Children's Theater - An Undergraduate Organization
description: The mission of Yale's Children's Theater is to share the joy of theatre arts with Yalies and New Haven youth.

name: Yale Civil Rights Project
description: The Yale Civil Rights Project is an organization for students working collaboratively with non-profit organizations such as the ACLU, Know Your IX, and National Employment Law Project on legal research projects related to civil rights in the areas of civil liberties, critical race theory, economic justice, LGBTQ rights, racial justice, and women's rights.

name: Yale Clean Energy Collaborative
description: Yale offers a wide range of campus-wide events for students interested in clean energy, and the Yale Clean Energy Collaborative is your one stop shop to experience them with like-minded peers! The Collaborative brings together students, faculty, staff, alumni, and online learners passionate about an equitable clean energy future. We host events and create community across campus and across the world with the goal of sharing knowledge, networks, and opportunities. Join our networking platform using your NetID and password at: https://community.cbey.yale.edu/login

name: Yale Club Cycling Team
description: To develop competitive and ethical racers, enthusiasm for riding, equality in racing, and foster a local biking community.

name: Yale Club Equestrian Team
description: The purpose of this team is to provide the opportunity for Yale students to compete in IHSA horse shows and to learn about equitation and horsemanship in a safe and supportive team environment.

name: Yale Club Indoor Climbing Team
description: YCT's mission is to provide a community for climbers at Yale and to provide resources for competition climbers at Yale. We welcome all students, regardless of prior experience, to join our team.

name: Yale Club Kendo Team
description: Yale Kendo seeks to teach the practice of Kendo in the Yale Community. Kendo (the way of the sword) is a martial art based on traditional Japanese swordmanship.

name: Yale Club Men's Soccer (C-2) Team
description: Our mission is to play the beautiful game beautifully while building a team whose chemistry transcends the boundaries of a soccer field.

name: Yale Club Men's Ultimate Frisbee Team - Süperfly
description: We are a sports team that exists to teach the sport of ultimate at a high level to all of our players, no matter what their athletic/ultimate backgrounds. Additionally, we strive to succeed competitively while staying true to the values of the international ultimate community that include gender equity and spirit of the game.

name: Yale Club Men's Water Polo Team
Yale Club Running Team
description: Yale Club Running welcomes all undergraduates (and graduate students) to run with us as a group. We offer multiple pace groups every day, and are far more focused on running together than running "fast." We do not hold try-outs, we do conduct organized -- and completely optional, occasionally overnight -- trips to cross country meets in the fall and track and marathon events in the spring. Track and other running workouts are held twice a week, but like all YCR events, workouts are totally optional. Alternate runs will always be available on workout days. We're a friendly group, with a wide ar

name: Yale Club Swim Team
description: Yale Club Swimming is a team of students from all corners of campus life, with any range of experience, who come together due to their love of swimming and the close-knit, family environment that they find.

name: Yale Club Tae Kwon Do Team
description: Club Taekwondo at Yale is a co-ed sports club that offers a dynamic Korean martial arts experience for undergraduate students, graduate students, and Yale faculty. Club TKD has operated for almost 40 years at Yale and provides a welcoming community and training environment where students can learn, grow, and compete at various levels of competition. Through rigorous training, members develop physical fitness, self-defense skills, and mental discipline. The club emphasizes technique, sparring, and forms to enhance students' overall athleticism and confidence.

name: Yale Club Triathlon Team
description: We are an all-inclusive group of undergraduate and graduate students who enjoy the sport of triathlon. We strive to create an environment where athletes of all skill levels can receive professional coaching and training in the sport they love. We also work hard to make an otherwise very expensive and elite sport affordable and accessible to students. Join us for fun swim/bike/run practices - no previous experience needed!

name: Yale Club Women's Rugby Team
description: We are the Yale Women's Rugby Football Club! We come from all walks of life, and all joined rugby with varying experience (majority had never played) but eager to meet new people, and learn a new sport with fitness-minded people. We like to say that we are the fittest team on campus :)

name: Yale Club Women's Ultimate Frisbee Team
Yale Club Women's Water Polo Team
Yale Club Wushu
description: The Yale Wushu team seeks to better its members in practice; by gaining focus and self-control through intense training. Members hope to achieve self-mastery that will translate into respect and compassion for others both inside and outside of the training hall. Yale Wushu also seeks to better its community. The Yale Wushu team has been blessed by many opportunities to spread the message of peace and nonviolence that lies at the center of the word "wushu." Our classmates at Yale will go on to be leaders in their respective fields; it is our hope that during our time here we succeed in spreadin

name: Yale College - Council of Heads of College
Yale College Anime Society
description: The purpose of the Yale College Anime Society is to allow people to appreciate East Asian culture--especially Japanese culture--through the lens of media and entertainment. We hope to give people the opportunity to explore genres and mediums they may have never explored. We primarily hope to do this through exposure to, discussion of, and analysis of Japanese Animation and Comics (i.e. "anime" and "manga"), Japanese music, and Japanese culture in general but will also look at manhwas, webtoons, light novels, and a variety of other mediums and genres . Through this, we aim to broaden the overal

name: Yale College Black Men's Student Union
description: The BMU's mission is to uplift and empower Black men on and off Yale's campus through our tenets of unity, support and service.

name: Yale College Chess Club
description: Yale College Chess Club promotes chess in the Yale-New Haven community through educational outreach and hosting tournaments. We furthermore represent Yale at intercollegiate chess competitions on the local, national, and international stages.

name: Yale College Class of 2026
description: Welcome to the Class of 2026! This portal will be your guide through the months ahead as you prepare to join us on campus. Here you will find important forms, deadlines, and a checklist to help you keep track of your required tasks.

name: Yale College Class of 2027
description: Welcome to the Class of 2027! This portal will be your guide through the months ahead as you prepare to join us on campus. Here you will find important forms, deadlines, and a checklist to help you keep track of your required tasks.

name: Yale College Council
description: The purpose of YCC shall be to pursue the improvement of the Yale undergraduate experience by lending a voice to student concerns and opinions, shaping University policy, protecting student rights and freedoms, promoting and financing undergraduate organizations, fostering school unity and pride, and serving as a forum for the discussion and advancement of student ideas. We shall serve as the primary liaison between the undergraduate student body and the administration, graduate schools, faculty, staff, alumni, and persons or groups outside of the University. Any issue affecting the quality of

name: Yale College Dean's Office Student Affairs
description: The Office of Student Affairs, located on the 2nd floor of 55 Whitney Avenue, provides critical support, advocacy, information, and guidance to undergraduates. Students are encouraged to seek the assistance of our office whenever needed.

name: Yale College Democrats
description: The Yale College Democrats are intentional advocates for progressive change in New Haven, in Connecticut, and across the country. We fight for candidates and causes that advance equal justice, human dignity, and the empowerment of historically marginalized communities. We embrace students of all backgrounds who want to take action and join a diverse community of dedicated progressives.

name: Yale College Republicans - A Student Organization
description: Republicans believe in liberty, economic prosperity, preserving American values and traditions, and restoring the American dream for every citizen of this great nation. As a party, we support policies that seek to achieve those goals. Our platform is centered on stimulating economic growth for all Americans, protecting constitutionally-guaranteed freedoms, ensuring the integrity of our elections, and maintaining our national security. We are working to preserve America's greatness for our children and grandchildren. The Republican Party's legacy -- we were originally founded in 1854 for the pu

name: Yale College Student Organization Officers
description: Yale College recognizes that organizations under the leadership of undergraduates can and do enhance a student's education by providing additional opportunities beyond the curriculum for personal development and growth. The Office of Student Affairs assists students in developing organizations and planning events, sometimes providing financial advice and assistance, clarifying University policies and procedures, and authorizing the use of University resources and facilities.

name: Yale College Student Organizations Consultants
description: Student Organizations Consultants (SOCs) work with the Office of Student Affairs in the Yale College Dean's Office to support undergraduate student organizations. SOCs serve as advisors, resources, and strategists for student organization officers registered with Yale College. Each SOC is assigned a caseload of student groups, organized by activity, that they assist over the course of the academic year.

name: Yale College Time Away Student Support
description: Yale College Time Away Student Support helps Yale College students navigate the leave and return process.

name: Yale Collegiate Chapter of the NAACP
description: Our mission is to achieve equity, political rights, and social inclusion by advancing policies and practices that expand human and civil rights, eliminate discrimination, and accelerate the well-being, education, and economic security of Black people and all persons of color.

name: Yale ColorStack - an Undergraduate Organization
description: ColorStack’s mission is to increase the number of Black and Latinx Computer Science graduates who go on to start rewarding technical careers. The organization is dedicated to providing educational resources, mentorship, and professional development opportunities to its members, thereby supporting their growth in the field of technology. ColorStack operates exclusively for charitable, educational, and scientific purposes under IRC Section 501(c)(3).

name: Yale Computer Society - an Undergraduate Organization
description: Yale's premier tech and computer science organization. Yale Computer Society exists to enrich the campus experience of tech and entrepreneurship by inspiring, informing, and engaging Yale students regarding applied computing.

name: Yale Concert Band
description: The Yale Bands is a thriving cultural community. Its members are given opportunities to prepare and perform great music; learn about the arts and their place in society and international cultures; and develop skills to become leaders. Through a robust series of musical activities, many Bands members work with and become serious performers, conductors, composers, arrangers, writers, archivists, historians, photographers, producers, choreographers, media producers, critics, and teachers. Band members develop and master these skills through service to the University, performing and producing comm

name: Yale Connect Admins Community of Practice
description: This group is for all Yale Connect System Administrators to test Yale Connect settings and features.

name: Yale Connect Ops Test Group
description: This is the mission

name: Yale Creative Society
description: YCS's mission is to provide space and community for aspiring creators of all kinds. Whether you create to publish, introspect, explore, dream, relax, tune out, tune in, or tune up, YCS is where you belong.

name: Yale Cushing Society
description: The mission of the Cushing Society is to foster a direct educational and research interface between Yale undergraduates, medical students, neurosurgery residents, and faculty. Through mentorship and collaboration, students can engage directly with neurosurgeons and scientists, building a supportive community that spans all levels of training. By connecting motivated students with basic science and clinical neurosurgery laboratories, the Cushing Society supports research initiatives that contribute to advancing the field.

name: Yale Dabke: An Undergraduate Organization
description: Yale Dabke's mission is to celebrate Levantine culture through dance and visual art. We honor our heritage by performing traditional Dabke and sharing its vibrant history. Our aim is to unite people in celebration of our rich traditions and spark creativity that inspires cultural dialogue.

name: Yale Danceworks - An Undergraduate Organization
description: Danceworks is committed to spreading the love of dance to everyone, catering to all styles and levels of experience, and giving everyone an opportunity to learn, improve, and perform!

name: Yale Debate Association - An Undergraduate Organization
description: As Yale's only competitive intercollegiate debating organization, we compete in the American Parliamentary style of debate as a member of the American Parliamentary Debate Association (APDA) and in the British Parliamentary style as a member of the US Universities Debating Association (USUDA). We represent Yale both across the country and around the world.

name: Yale Democracy Project
description: The Yale Democracy Project is a non-partisan organization that strives to increase civic engagement among all Yalies, defend student voting rights, and make the voting process as accessible as possible. We understand that to live in a democracy is to live in a society that honors the liberty and dignity of all people. We advocate on behalf of democratic practices and principles with this broad understanding of democracy in mind.

name: Yale Dhvani - a Student Group for Classical Indian Music
description: Yale Dhvani aims to promote Classical Indian music on campus in the forms of Carnatic and Hindustani styles, both vocal and instrumental. Through rehearsals and performances, the club serves to enhance individual classical styles while harmoniously integrating multiple distinct styles in a "jugalbandhi."

name: Yale Digital Ethics Center
description: We research the governance, ethical, legal, and social implications of digital innovation and technologies and their human, societal, and environmental impact.

name: Yale Discolf! Undergraduate Group
description: Our mission is to promote the growing sport of disc golf in the Yale community and beyond. We aim to make the sport more accessible to those familiar with it and excitedly introduce it to those eager to learn about it for the first time. We meet casually for a round of disc golf every week either on campus or at a local public course to make the most of the sport’s inherent community dynamic, to savor the gorgeous New England outdoors, and to chuck frisbees, in a perfect world, right down the center of the fairway.

name: Yale Divinity Library
description: The Yale Divinity Library supports teaching and research in disciplines related to Christianity with particular strength in Bible, theology, and the history of Christianity. The Day Missions Collection is the strongest collection of its kind anywhere in the world. The Ministry Resource Center houses material supporting the practice of ministry.

name: Yale Divinity School Korean Students Association (YDSKA)
description: The Yale Divinity School Korean Association (YDSKA) includes individuals at YDS who identify themselves as Korean, Korean-American, or Korean-related, and who are also engaging in or practicing their lives within a global context. This organization advocates for the development and preservation of its cultural identities through various activities. Our gatherings provide a secure environment for sharing personal experiences related to integrating Korean culture and heritage into both religious and academic settings at Yale Divinity School and beyond.

name: Yale Divinity Student Government
description: The purpose of the Student Government shall be the following: To act as the legislative assembly of the student body of Yale Divinity School (the "Divinity School" or "YDS"). To serve as the primary representative of the student body before the faculty and administration of the Divinity School. To act on behalf of the students and their interests on issues of YDS policy and community concern. To advocate for the interests of the Divinity School students within the broader Yale University community.

name: Yale Dominican Student Association
description: DSA was founded with the intent of spreading awareness concerning the Dominican experience and culture. These goals shall be met through: (a) Sponsoring informative and social events that will aid in addressing issues concerning Dominicans and other Latinos. These events shall be open to the entire Yale and New Haven community. (b) Concentrating its efforts on recruitment and retention of Dominican students by developing academic and personal support networks for undergraduate students, and establishing networks with professionals and DSA alumni. (c) Striving to serve Dominican communities in

name: Yale Drama Coalition: An Undergraduate Organization
description: In order to foster communication and collaboration within the undergraduate theater community and provide resources to students who wish to enhance their theatrical experience, the Yale Drama Coalition (YDC) is dedicated to acting as an organizational body in support of the performance community at Yale. We seek to both offer support for individual productions and also advocate on behalf of the theater community before the Yale administration.

name: Yale Effective Altruism Student Group
description: To spread the ideas of effective altruism through analysis, outreach, advocacy, education and collaboration, and to engage with and enable effective altruistic practice using the immense resources and opportunities available at Yale. We aim to help facilitate students to find effective charities and enter careers that do a significant amount of good.

name: Yale Emergency Medical Services – an Undergraduate Organization
description: The purpose of this organization is to create a safer and healthier campus environment by providing comprehensive training in emergency medical care and by reducing morbidity and mortality.

name: Yale Entertainment and Sports Law Association
description: The Yale Entertainment and Sports Law Association (YESLA) endeavors to expose members and the broader YLS community to important legal topics in the Sports and Entertainment industries. YESLA plans to host a number of speakers and organize trips to various events.

name: Yale Entrepreneurial Society – an Undergraduate Organization
description: The Yale Entrepreneurial Society is an undergraduate organization that aims to cultivate a cohesive and supportive community of entrepreneurs by showcasing, connecting, and aiding students interested in the entrepreneurial scene at Yale and beyond.

name: Yale Environment 360 Magazine
description: Yale Environment 360 is an online magazine offering opinion, analysis, reporting, and debate on global environmental issues. We feature original articles by scientists, journalists, environmentalists, academics, policy makers, and business people, as well as multimedia content and a daily digest of major environmental news.

name: Yale Environment Review
description: Yale Environment Review (YER) is a student-run review that provides weekly updates on environmental research findings. YER aims to bridge the gap between environmentally-related academic research and its application to policy and management. In order to increase access to specialized information, YER publishes readable and concise summaries of original, peer-reviewed literature so that it can be useful to those engaged in the field of environmental and natural resource management.

name: Yale Environment Women SIG (YEW)
description: We aim to support, platform, and connect women in environmental science throughout their journey at YSE, empowering them to understand and advocate for women's rights and justice in the face of anthropogenic climate threats.

name: Yale Environmental Dialogue
description: Injecting new energy and fresh thinking into the national conversation about sustainability. Learn more here: https://environment.yale.edu/dialogue

name: Yale Environmental Law Association (SIG)
description: The Yale Environmental + Energy Law Association (YELA) aims to build community among YSE and YLS students interested in the environmental/energy law and policy. YELA seeks to draw attention to all aspects of our natural and built environment through community events, panels and reading groups, and opportunities to serve historically marginalized and frontline communities in the fight for environmental justice. We welcome everyone to join us, regardless of prior environmental background or experience.

name: Yale Environmental Law Association (YELA)
description: The Yale Environmental Law Association (YELA) provides a home for students interested in environmental law and concerned about the climate crisis. YELA draws attention to all aspects of environmental law, environmental justice, and related fields through YLS community events, speakers and reading groups, and opportunities to connect and collaborate with other campus groups. YELA also serves as a hub for climate and environmental activism at YLS and beyond. YELA places special emphasis on the interdisciplinary, multifaceted character of environmental law and its relevance to a wide range of leg

name: Yale Ethiopian and Eritrean Students Association
description: Provide a space that brings together the Ethiopian and Eritrean community including the diaspora community at Yale to celebrate our shared culture, history and language and engage in conversations of social, political and economic issues affecting our countries.

name: Yale European Graduate Student Society
description: We bring together European students and European culture enthusiasts at the graduate and professional level at Yale for the purpose of fostering friendships, networking, and discussion. This group serves both as an informal and formal way to network, meet speakers, and have conversations about topics related to Europe.

name: Yale Existential Risks Initiative - An Undergraduate Organization
description: The Yale Existential Risks Initiative (YERI) raises awareness and cultivates advocacy among students at Yale University around global issues that pose existential threats to humanity, with special emphasis on nuclear warfare, biological terrorism, artificial intelligence disasters, and the intersection of these issues with each other and the climate crisis. By spreading and centralizing the insight of policymakers, academics, and organizers on these issues, YERI aims to inspire Yale students to help prevent the man-made end of humanity as we know it, and to open concrete pathways to do so.

name: Yale Federalist Society
description: The Federalist Society is founded on three core principles: We believe that the state exists to preserve freedom. We believe that the separation of governmental powers is central to our Constitution. And we believe that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is, not what it should be.

name: Yale Film Archive
description: The Yale Film Archive, part of the Yale University Library, advances film culture across campus and around the world through collection, preservation, access, and exhibition.

name: Yale Film Society: a student organization
description: The Yale Film Society is dedicated to the appreciation and presentation of films on campus for students by students. The Yale Film Society's main offerings include hosting and promoting screenings, social networking events between Yale student cinephiles, and the publication of a biweekly newsletter promoting film-related events around campus, announcing upcoming screenings, and publishing YFS content.

name: Yale First-Gen and/or Low-income Advocacy Movement - A Student Group
description: We are a coalition dedicated to advocacy and community-building for all First-gen and/or low-income students at Yale. Throughout the year, we form task forces based on the projects that members want to work on, such as FGLI student-faculty mixers, financial aid literacy, and advocating for a FGLI-dedicated space on campus. In the midst of all of this advocacy, we also make sure to foster a safe space for FGLI folks to bond and form deeper relationships - if we don't support each other, who will?

name: Yale Fold Student Club
description: We are interested in investigating the geometric maneuver of folding and all the disparate places it manages to show up, across disciplines and subjects of inquiry. We aim to transcend the lines of disciplines, and create a space where diverse ideas can be unified under the common theme of folding. Yale Fold Student Club will be a place where people can share their enthusiasms, learn from others, and relax with friends over origami and croissants.

name: Yale Foreign Policy Initiative - An Undergraduate Organization
description: The Yale Foreign Policy Initiative (YFPI) is a student-run organization dedicated to the creation of comprehensive and research-backed solutions to tackle the world's leading foreign affairs issues. Partnering with think tanks, government agencies, and the Jackson School in pursuit of policy research, YFPI seeks to prepare generations of Yale undergraduates for careers in foreign service and international relations.

name: Yale Forest Forum
description: The Yale Forest Forum offers weekly lunch talks during the academic year, providing opportunities to hear from leaders in forest management, conservation, or policy in an informal setting. The YFF speaker series is the longest continuously-running speaker series at the Yale School of the Environment. Speakers come from a wide range of organizations and perspectives, including government, NGOs and businesses, working at scales from local to international.

name: Yale Forests
description: Yale Forests is a living laboratory for teaching, management, and research, stewarding 10,592 acres of forestland across three New England states.

name: Yale Friends of Israel: An Undergraduate Organization
description: Yale Friends of Israel seeks to bring Israeli society, culture, and politics to campus, and encourages open dialogue about Israel's domestic and international politics. We seek to foster a community of Yale students who are passionate about Israel and the Middle East.

name: Yale Funbotics - an Undergraduate Organization
description: Our mission is to introduce robotics to the underprivileged youth in New Haven and encourage imagination and teamwork. By providing an early, hands-on look into engineering, Funbotics aims to drive more children into STEM fields from a young age. Through our program, students not only learn the foundations of robotics and develop critical thinking, team-building, and presentation skills, but they also are exposed to the fun in robotics and STEM.

name: Yale Fuzhounese Students Association
description: The Yale Fuzhounese Students Association (YFSA) aims to shine a light on the experiences of Fuzhounese students and families, uplifting a community often overlooked within broader Chinese and Asian American narratives. YFSA addresses issues unique to Fuzhounese and other working-class immigrant communities, including endangered language access, intergenerational gaps, and the erasure of Fuzhounese diasporic migration and labor histories. Through mentorship, professional development, and connections to Fuzhounese individuals and students in New York City, YFSA fosters solidarity, cultural under

name: Yale Glee Club
description: The Yale Glee Club is Yale's principal undergraduate mixed choir and oldest musical organization, currently in its 160th season. Our plans for Fall 2020: Like choirs throughout the world, we will not be able to do many of the things we normally do this coming fall, but we are committed to maintaining the Glee Club as a vibrant community for Yale students who love to sing by making music together however we can, learning, serving our community, and cultivating connections with each other.

name: Yale Government Relations Group - An Undergraduate Organization
description: The Yale Undergraduate Government Relations Group seeks to equip Yale undergraduates with the knowledge and skills to navigate lobbying and legislative advocacy. The Group aims to foster civic engagement and empower students to influence the political process and drive meaningful change.

name: Yale Grad Crew
description: Yale Grad Crew (YGC) brings together members from across Yale's graduate and professional schools. As a co-ed club, YGC welcomes both experienced rowers and novices, creating an inclusive environment where athletes of all skill levels can learn, train, and compete together. Each year, the team introduces a new class of novice rowers to the sport through structured coaching and on-the-water instruction, while experienced athletes continue to develop their skills through regular practices and competitive racing. YGC regularly participates in some of the nation's most prestigious head races, incl

name: Yale Grad Sailing
description: The purpose of the Club is to foster a community of graduate and professional students from various schools within Yale University who share an interest in sailing. The Club aims to: 1. Promote the sport and joy of sailing among graduate students. 2. Provide educational opportunities for members to learn and improve their sailing skills. 3. Organize sailing-related activities, including but not limited to, sailing trips, competitions, and social events. 4. Ensure a welcoming and inclusive environment for students of all skill levels, from beginners to advanced sailors.

name: Yale Graduate Foosball Club
description: The Yale Graduate Foosball Club (YGFC) is a graduate and professional student organization open to all students interested in foosball. YGFC offers an opportunity to connect with peers from various departments and schools in a relaxed and social environment. Through casual foosball games and tournaments, members enjoy both friendly competition and the chance to build new friendships across the Yale community.

name: Yale Graduate Muslim Students Association
description: The Yale Graduate Muslim Students Association provides those who are affiliated with the University in a post-undergraduate capacity a space to interact and socialize with other Muslim-identifying people on campus. The Yale Graduate Muslim Students Association is committed to fostering a sense of community across the University's many graduate and professional schools. This group is open to all interested students!

name: Yale Graduate Rugby Football Club
description: This club has active Men's and Women's teams and provides the opportunity to break out of the bubble of your graduate program and make friends from all the other graduate schools, as well as meeting graduate students from around the world on the teams we play against, all while competing in one of the world's greatest sports - rugby. Each year, YGRFC participates in some of the greatest Rugby Tournaments across the country, including Hogfest at Wharton in the fall, as well as the MBA Rugby World Cup in New York in the spring.

name: Yale Graduate Society of Women Engineers
description: The Graduate Society of Women Engineers (gradSWE) is a forum to connect grad students interested in the inclusion of women in engineering within the broader engineering community. Through our activities, we seek to provide both personal and professional development, in order to support female engineering students on the path to an advanced degree and in their careers after graduating.

name: Yale Graduate Student Art and Creative Writing Society at YSPH
parent: Yale School of Public Health Student Organizations
description: The Yale School of Public Health Arts & Creative Writing Society aims to foster creativity, community, and personal expression among students by creating opportunities to engage with the arts and share creative work. The Society provides a welcoming, inclusive space for students to explore their creative interests, connect with others who share those interests, and enrich their experience at YSPH through the arts and creative writing. While the Society is primarily designed for Executive MPH students, all YSPH students are welcome!

name: Yale Graduate Student Christian Fellowship
description: We are a community of Christians who encourage one another in developing our gifts, education and passions to glorify God in our current scholarship and future professions. We seek to engage other graduate students and the broader Yale and New Haven communities with Christ's message of God's love that renews and redeems the world. As an affiliated chapter of the Graduate and Faculty Ministry (GFM) of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship, we also embrace their mission statement, which is: The mission of GFM is to encourage and equip graduate students and faculty to follow Christ as they seek to be

name: Yale Graduate Student Consulting Club
description: Our mission at the YGCC is to provide a platform for Yale graduate students to learn about and prepare for productive careers in management consulting by transforming Yale into a prime recruiting ground for top firms.

name: Yale Graduate Student Tennis and Golf Club at YSPH
parent: Yale School of Public Health Student Organizations
description: YSPH's Yale Graduate Student Tennis & Golf Club aims to foster community, friendship, and well-being among students by creating opportunities to connect with others through recreational tennis and golf. The club provides a welcoming, inclusive avenue for students to find playing partners, enjoy time outdoors, and support their well-being through recreational sports. While this is an initiative primarily designed for Executive MPH students, all are welcome!

name: Yale GSAS BIPOC Graduate Collective
description: The Yale GSAS BIPOC Grad Collective (BIPOC-GC) is a graduate student interdisciplinary, social affinity and professional development organization that brings together graduate students, community members, and faculty members from diverse disciplinary, racial, and ethnic backgrounds who might otherwise not have the opportunity to meet. YHeLPS invites speakers, plans career info sessions and networking events, organizes experiential learning opportunities like the medical-legal partnerships, and coordinates with other health organizations throughout Yale University.

description: We invite graduate students across Yale to attend monthly zoom talks where nationally renowned health policy experts discuss their newly published research.

We connect entrepreneurial undergraduate students with founders within the Yale and New Haven community, and beyond. Our dedicated students help startups achieve milestones and drive growth. Last year, we successfully supported 45startups and are eager to continue this success into the 2026-2027 academic year.

We organize events throughout the year to promote an awareness of Hinduism within the Yale and New Haven community. Our events are meant to stimulate an exchange of ideas on religion, and are above all, educational.

Hospitality creates spaces where community thrives, ideas are shared, and traditions begin. Law students engage in projects involving direct legal services, assisting with strategic litigation, and drafting appeals of immigration decisions. As they stand, immigration policies exist to disorient and dehumanize those who wish to make their home in the U.S. We envision a different future in which no one has to live in fear because of their documentation status. description: The expanding impact investment market channels capital into critical sectors like renewable energy, healthcare, and microfinance. description: Our club, the Yale Innovators Network, strives to serve the Yale entrepreneurial community by providing high-quality, informative, multimedia content meant to showcase the work of student founders across Yale’s undergraduate and graduate programs. This media content is not only meant to serve as a medium for startup founders to expand their audience by reaching out to other Yale students and young entrepreneurs, but also to give these entrepreneurs an insight into the life and work that is needed to be successful at a startup, as well as the kinds of ideas and markets that can be tapped into.

We also explore the impact of our research and of synthetic biology as a field through community engagement.

description: The Yale Journal of International Affairs (YJIA) is a graduate student-run journal that aims to publish the best student and practitioner writing on international affairs. YJIA engages with the richness of its subject matter by elevating distinct perspectives and diverse areas of expertise among its writers and its editorship. description: The Yale Journal of Law and Feminism is committed to publishing scholarship on gender, sexuality, and the law, especially insofar as the law structures, affects, or ignores the experiences of women and other marginalized peoples. name: Yale Journal of Law and Technology
description: The Yale Journal of Law and Technology (YJoLT) offers a network of tech-focused law students and exposure to cutting-edge legal scholarship. If you are passionate about robotics, science, privacy and beyond, join our community!

description: The Yale Journal on Regulation (JREG) is a biannual student-edited law review covering regulatory, administrative, corporate law topics. It is the top-ranked journal in the fields of corporate, administrative, bankruptcy, and commercial law in the United States.

The YJI team provides career guidance, organizes events with inspiring journalists, and offers programming to support students in their journalistic ambitions. MMATHS is a collaboration between Yale, University of Michigan, University of Texas-Dallas, University of Iowa, University of Florida, Oakton College, USC, and the University of Maryland, while Girls in Math strives to provide a welcoming experience non-binary and female-identifying students, as well as any other students who identify with underrepresented gender minorities in mathematics.

Our goal is to conduct research on oil production and develop qualitative and quantitative models regarding the oil market. Within our group, we strive to foster an inclusive community, where people representing different backgrounds come together and sing in harmony. We aim to maintain a diverse repertoire of songs to include not only varying genres, but also artists of color.

name: Yale Outdoors
description: Yale Outdoors serves the Yale community with high-quality and safe trips to explore the outdoors and develop wilderness skills. Yale Outdoors creates a community for students to meet and learn from others who are interested in the outdoors hoping to make the outdoors accessible to all at Yale. We provide affordable wilderness skills training sessions and outdoors equipment for the Yale community. Above all, Yale Outdoors spreads the love for the outdoors and appreciation for nature with the rest of the Yale community.

We aim to introduce padel to newcomers, offering expert instruction and a supportive learning environment. We value holistic, patient-centered care that respects the diverse priorities and identities of our patients. We strive to lessen gaps in current medical practice by encouraging communication and collaboration between patients, students, and healthcare and community-based resource providers.

To this end, we speak about science at venues ranging from libraries to local bars across New Haven and beyond. As Yale graduate students and postdoctoral scholars, we have a responsibility to make science accessible to the general public, especially to under-served communities. We believe that anyone can engage with science and use it in their lives.

Our mission is to engage students with alumni for life and career wisdom, networking opportunities, and fun, fostering lifelong connections and enriching their Yale experience.

description: To appreciate, discuss, research, and document the architectural heritage at Yale - that is, in and around the Yale campus. This will consist of regular meetings for members, architecturally-oriented group perambulations, and research/cataloging of interesting features

name: Yale Student Association for Small Claims Assistance
description: The Yale Student Association for Small Claims Assistance (Y-SASCA) is an organization based in New Haven that seeks to provide legal information to individuals navigating the small claims court system in Connecticut. We hope to assist clients in effectively obtaining legal remedies while safeguarding their rights as consumers, tenants, and valued community members.

name: Yale Student Bowling Association
description: The mission of the Yale Student Bowling Association is to create an inclusive, accessible, and community-driven space for Yale students to learn, practice, and enjoy the sport of bowling. We aim to foster both recreational and competitive engagement by connecting students of all experience levels through regular open-bowl sessions, practices, and social events, while also encouraging academic and cultural exploration of the sport through watch parties, discussions of professional bowling, and conversations about the physics and artistry behind the game, building a community rooted in curiosity

name: Yale Student Branch of the IEEE
description: Y-IEEE's mission is to promote Electrical Engineering at the intersection of liberal arts and technology via exciting projects and inspiring events. We envision a vibrant, spontaneous, and ambitious culture of engineering at Yale.

name: Yale Student Chapter of Project Sunshine

name: Yale Student Chapter of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers
description: The purpose of this Chapter is to promote knowledge of chemical engineering and to promote mutual acquaintance and good fellowship among Yale chemical engineering students and between students and instructors, and to provide services when called upon in order to present a good image of the University to the community. name: Yale Student Environmental Coalition
description: Empower students to engage in all forms of environmental activism on campus, in New Haven, and beyond. Foster a sense of community around people and earth at Yale, uniting networks of environmentalists as well as providing opportunities for students of all backgrounds to engage and share their perspectives on environmental issues.

name: Yale Student Film Festival
description: The Yale Student Film Festival (YSFF) is a platform that uplifts unique student voices from around the world. We seek to amplify stories that only students can tell, and build global and local communities of young filmmakers who can support each other as they enter the entertainment industry.

name: Yale Student Fragrance Organization
description: The Yale Student Fragrance Organization is Yale's first and only club that gives students a platform to create and engage with perfumes & fragrances. Join us to create your signature scent in one of our workshops!

name: Yale Student Klezmer Band
description: The Yale Student Klezmer Band aims to spread appreciation for Klezmer by teaching its members to be Klezmer musicians and by hosting performances throughout the year.

name: Yale Student Lettuce Club
description: The Yale Student Lettuce Club aims to promote the creation of lettuce-positive culture at Yale as an essential part of students' physical, emotional, and spiritual well-being. Through events like the annual lettuce eating competition and the all-nighter arts festival, we foster lettuce awareness on campus and beyond. We welcome all members of the Yale community to join us in our mission. Ranch not included.

name: Yale Student Magic: the Gathering Club
description: Yale Student Magic: the Gathering Club seeks to promote and facilitate the card game Magic: the Gathering within the Yale-New Haven community and to provide a space for learning, friendly competition, and collaboration.

name: Yale Student Mental Health Association
description: The Yale Student Mental Health Association, a student organization at Yale, works to increase mental health awareness, education and advoacy by collaborating with Yale administration on related policies and providing resources for the Yale and Greater New Haven community.

name: Yale Student Musicians United in Service and Empowerment
description: Yale MUSE strives to bring the healing power of live instrumental music directly into healthcare settings by partnering with the music volunteer program at Yale New Haven Hospital. We serve patients, families, and healthcare staff by providing bedside performances, larger atrium benefit concerts to support hospital research initiatives, and interactive music experiences that promote connection and emotional well-being.

description: The Yale Student Puzzle Club aims to promote puzzles, puzzle hunts, and related activities at Yale. We hope to host collaborative puzzle-solving events for large annual puzzle hunts such as the MIT Mystery Hunt, Galactic Puzzle Hunt, CMU Puzzle Hunt, Brown Puzzle Hunt, and other similar events, as well as increasing awareness and interest in puzzle hunting at Yale. We also hope to write and host an online puzzle hunt as a club, which will be open to everyone interested in participating.

name: Yale Student Quantitative Finance Organization
description: To cultivate a dynamic and inclusive community for undergraduate students passionate about the intersection of finance, mathematics, and technology. Our mission is to: 1. Educate: Provide members with a robust understanding of quantitative finance through workshops, seminars, and guest lectures from industry experts. 2. description: The Yale Student UFO Society aims to contribute to the scientific research surrounding the UAP enigma by conducting rigorous research, promoting responsible dialogue, and creating an inclusive space for people to discuss the mysteries of unidentified flying objects.

name: Yale Student Valorant Club
description: Our mission is to bring the world of esports and gaming into Yale through a Valorant organization. Esports is a growing phenomenon in the world, and Yale students should have the opportunity to join this impactful and teamwork-oriented hobby and environment. In Yale Valorant, students will learn how to work together and play as a team both casually and maybe competitively, gaining important life skills through the world of esports.

name: Yale Student-Athletes in Finance
description: Our mission is to empower student-athletes to leverage their unique skills to break into the world of finance by learning the necessary steps to secure top internships through hands-on mentorship and exclusive events.

name: Yale Students for a National Health Program
description: Yale Students for a National Health Program (SNaHP) hopes to represent future physicians in advocating for a federally-funded universal healthcare system, in addition to providing a space for all students to participate in conversations and debate about these policy solutions. We collaborate with our allies at the national SNaHP organization, as well as Physicians for a National Health Program (PNHP).

name: Yale Students for Christ
description: The purpose of Yale Students for Christ (YSC) is live out faith, hope, and love in our campus, city, and world. We aim to provide an environment where Christian students can articulate and live out their faith collectively in a campus setting, and where any students can explore the Christian faith.

description: Yale Students for Ranked Choice Voting is a nonpartisan organization dedicated to promoting awareness of ranked choice voting (RCV) in the Yale community and beyond. In doing so, we seek to rally support for this reform, which will reduce the temperature of our bitter political climate and make elections more truly democratic and representative of the diversity of identities and ideas of the population as a whole.

name: Yale Students for Reproductive Rights
description: Yale Students for Reproductive Rights is committed to building an informed, supportive, and engaged campus community around reproductive health, rights, and technologies. We aim to make conversations about reproductive justice more accessible—creating space for students to learn, ask questions, and connect across different perspectives and experiences. description: YSIG is an organization for Yale Medical School students interested in exploring careers in surgery and its subspecialties. With support from the Department of Surgery, students are afforded the opportunity to become junior members of the surgical community.

name: Yale Sustainable Food Program
description: On the farm, in the classroom, and around the world, the Yale Sustainable Food Program grows food-literate leaders.

name: Yale Symphony Orchestra
description: The Yale Symphony Orchestra (YSO) is an inclusive organization that is committed to elevating the musical discourse at Yale by sharing an exciting annual program of high-quality performances, workshops, and social activities.

name: Yale Taiwanese Student Association
description: We are a student association run by Taiwanese graduate students and postdocs to improve our networking and provide supports. We hold some social events like board game weekend or hot pot parties to strengthen our connection. All groups are open to all interested students!

We are dedicated to promoting inclusivity, academic success, and personal growth among transfer students, and we welcome all new members to join us in our mission.

name: Yale Ultramarathon Student Organization
description: Yale's Ultramarathon Club is open to all undergraduate and graduate students interested in ultrarunning regardless of experience. Ultrarunning entails running for distances further than a marathon, spanning up to multi-day, continuous running endeavors where one's will to keep moving forward supersedes all other predisposed genetic and skill factors. We host regular group workouts and events, as well as meetings and guest speakers to discuss training, nutrition, gear, and race strategies to grow the sport throughout the Yale community.

name: Yale Ultrasound Interest Group / Yale POCUS Interest Group

description: This student organization seeks to develop the resources, community, and support for aspiring student actuaries and undergraduates interested in or seeking to pursue actuarial science, the study of risk management and its application to companies and clients. For company members, this includes not only weekly practice of ballet technique, but also choreographic opportunities and performances. The goal of the company is to successfully teach students about ballet and provide a space for students to practice and improve their technique, while also keeping them excited and engaged about the art form.

YCEDS aims to provide club members access to laboratory space, faculty mentorship and inter-collegiate engineering competitions in order to explore engineering principles in vastly exciting ways. description: The Yale Undergraduate Chess Team (YUCT) strives to build a community of excellence by uniting Yale’s strongest chess players to compete at the highest levels, represent Yale with distinction, and inspire the broader chess community. description: The Yale Coffee Club (YCoC) is a student organization focused on the appreciation and study of coffee, from its origins and production methods to the brewing process. description: YUDI (Yale Undergraduate Diversified Investments) is Yale's largest undergraduate finance group and the only group focused primarily on investment banking and private equity. We provide a rigorous educational curriculum, personalized mentorship, exclusive networking events, M&A case competitions, and firm visits that will ensure your placement at a top firm.

name: Yale Undergraduate Dungeons and Dragons Organization
description: The Yale Undergraduate Dungeons and Dragons Organization is a community dedicated to the game and the art of Dungeons and Dragons and other TTRPGs, promoted to the skills of leadership, communication, and team-building it builds, with love for the lifelong friendships tables can spark. We roll together.

description: Club EnvE is dedicated to creating an inclusive and diverse community of students interested in Environmental Engineering and related subjects, cultivating a network of future engineers who address environmental challenges with a commitment to equity and sustainability.

name: Yale Undergraduate Fiber Arts and Crafting Society
description: The Yale Undergraduate Fiber Arts and Crafting Society seeks to bring Yale College students together through a shared love of the crafting arts. This is a club meant for people of all levels, from absolute novices to expert crafters. This group emphasizes the importance of learning, teaching, and growing together, both in terms of artistic ability as well as emotional fulfillment. description: Spreading the Gospel of Jesus Christ through song.

description: The Yale Undergraduate Hedge Fund Association (YUHA) serves as an interactive and inclusive platform to connect students and alumni with a shared interest in finance. YUHA was formed to provide curious students with an opportunity to learn about a sector that typically excludes undergraduates and aims to strengthen Yalie connections, current and past through firm visits, workshops, networking events, and informational literature. description: The Yale Undergraduate Hispanic Pre-Law Association (YUHPLA) is a Yale College student-led organization with the purpose of educating and empowering Hispanic undergraduates along their journey to law school. description: The Yale Undergraduate Humanities in Medicine Celebrations is concerned with promoting innovation at the intersection of the Humanities and the Medical fields. Yale HuMed provides space for students, faculty, and alumni to connect and celebrate achievements and engage in conversation on the art of medical humanities. HuMed will host an annual symposium Celebration event hosting at least one Yale College alumnus to speak about the intersection of medicine and the humanities. The organization will form a publication to highlight student artwork and writing on the topic of medicine and health.

description: Yale Jashan Bhangra is a dance troupe that celebrates the vibrant South Asian dance known as bhangra. Our purpose is to connect the greater Yale population to the fun, colorful traditions of South Asia through on-campus performances, workshops, and cultural events.

name: Yale Undergraduate Jazz Collective
description: The Yale Undergraduate Jazz Collective aims to foster a community around jazz music on campus. We host concerts, discussions, jam sessions, and masterclasses to establish both performance and educational opportunities for students and members of the New Haven community. In addition, we lobby for a formal jazz curriculum at Yale.

description: The Yale Kalaa is a hub through which undergraduate and graduate dancers trained in Indian classical styles, including Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi, and Kathak styles, practice and perform for various events on campus. 'Kalaa' (pronounced "kuh-laa") is a Sanskrit word meaning "a skilled craft." Through Yale Kalaa, we use our craft to celebrate and share the joy of classical Indian dance.

name: Yale Undergraduate Law Journal
description: The Yale Undergraduate Law Journal is a student-written and student-run journal of legal scholarship. name: Yale Undergraduate Learn to Skate Program
description: Our organization provides an after-school program for local New Haven elementary school children to learn how to ice skate. We give experienced skaters at Yale the opportunity to teach skating lessons to program participants.

name: Yale Undergraduate Legal Aid Association
description: The Yale Undergraduate Legal Aid Association is an organization open to young, human rights and legal aid-interested undergraduate students, which focuses primarily on offering its members volunteer opportunities on various legal projects in the greater New Haven area throughout the semester. We also organize advocacy events on campus to expand awareness on legal issues that pertain especially to the criminal justice system, immigration, refugee resettlement, and asylum-seeking.

name: Yale Undergraduate Mathematics Society
description: The Yale Undergraduate Mathematics Society, or YUMS, aims to create and foster a community for undergraduates at Yale interested in mathematics. It does so by hosting a number of events for math students, including colloquia, study sessions, game nights, and panels about the math major and summer opportunities.

name: Yale Undergraduate Mock Trial Association
description: The Yale College Mock Trial Association is an undergraduate organization that seeks to promote student interest and knowledge in the law and the American judicial system through participation in intercollegiate mock trial competition.

name: Yale Undergraduate Moot Court Team
description: We are a team of undergraduate students at Yale University who are passionate about the law. Our team members have a wide variety of interests and majors, but we all enjoy preparing for and competing in the American Moot Court Association Competition each year. We love teaching anyone we can about how interesting and important moot court and the law are. If you're interested in getting involved in moot court, you'll find many more resources on this website, or you can contact us directly!

name: Yale Undergraduate Music Mentorship Initiative
description: Yale Undergraduate Music Mentorship Initiative (YUMMI) is a new student-led organization dedicated to expanding access to music education for New Haven youth. Founded on the belief that music is a powerful tool for creativity and community, YUMMI connects Yale student musicians with local public school students for personalized, one-on-one instruction.

name: Yale Undergraduate Net Impact
description: Yale Undergraduate Net Impact (YUNI) is an on-campus consulting firm working for socially responsible businesses, ranging in size from Fortune 500 companies to not-for-profits. Net Impact's semester-long consulting projects are professional, in-depth efforts that provide lasting value to our clients, for whom we tackle the toughest business challenges.

name: Yale Undergraduate Philosophy Review
description: The Yale Philosophy Review (YPR) is an annual journal dedicated to publishing philosophical writing by undergraduates worldwide.

name: Yale Undergraduate Photography Society
description: The Yale Undergraduate Photography Society aims to share the vast photographic resources on campus, display student work, advise beginners, and serve as a network for student photographers.

name: Yale Undergraduate Piano Collective
description: One of the hallmarks of Yale College is its renowned musical community. Outstanding instrumental musicians on campus frequently perform together in such well-regarded ensembles as the Yale Symphony Orchestra and the Yale Concert Band. Pianists, however, are required only in small numbers for these groups and may therefore find themselves somewhat isolated in their musical pursuit. name: Yale Undergraduate Pizza Society
description: The Yale Undergraduate Pizza Society (YUPS) seeks to explore the history and tradition of pizza within the Yale and New Haven communities. Students in the organization will have a space to share their love of pizza through discussions, presentations, articles, and field trips. Above all, the Yale Pizza Society strives to create a greater sense of appreciation for the one-of-a-kind pizza culture that exists in New Haven.

name: Yale Undergraduate Poker Club
description: Welcome to Yale Student Poker Club, a welcoming environment of quantitative, risk-tolerant, and friendly individuals who happen to love playing cards. Throughout the year, we run weekly live games, freeroll tournaments, poker workshops, and compete in intercollegiate poker tournaments. We grow together as decision-makers with analytical approaches to the game, constantly seeking ways to improve our edge. YPC welcomes poker players of all levels. Whether you are a seasoned player or simply interested in the game, join us!

name: Yale Undergraduate Political Association
description: The Yale Undergraduate Political Association (YUPA), aims to promote political engagement, foster bipartisan dialogue, provide opportunities for political research and advocacy, and cultivate a community of students interested in politics.

description: Our mission is to promote and facilitate the participation of undergraduates in quantum information science at Yale, to contribute to the larger community studying quantum information science, and to connect Yalies to the rapidly-growing quantum information science industry.

description: The Yale Undergraduate Research Journal elevates undergraduate research at Yale through a student-run, peer-reviewed publication. In so doing, it showcases original scholarship across disciplines and promotes a campus culture of rigorous inquiry.

The Texas Club strives to foster relationships between both Texan and non-Texan students to honor and celebrate the history of Texas.
