description: Yale Undergraduates at Connecticut Hospice (YUCH) is an organization that provides the unique opportunity to work at a palliative care facility a short drive away from campus in Branford, CT. Volunteers provide a service that is crucial to the Hospice organization and uplifting to the patients. There are a variety of volunteer departments ranging from patient assistance to art therapy, which all immerse volunteers in the real patient care experience.

name: Yale University Art Gallery
description: The Yale University Art Gallery collects, preserves, studies, and presents art in all media, from all regions of the globe and across time. The museum’s exceptional collection—numbering over 300,000 objects—is the core of its identity. It sustains and catalyzes all we do. Founded in 1832, the Gallery is the oldest university art museum in America. Today, it is a center for teaching, learning, and scholarship and is a preeminent cultural asset for Yale University, the wider academic community, and the public. The museum is open to all, free of charge, and is committed to engaging audiences thro

name: Yale University Chaplain's Office
description: This is a word that we in the Yale University Chaplain's Office use and enthusiastically commit to putting into practice often. The very foundation of the work that we do at Yale is about creating an environment that feels welcoming to all people. Whether you are part of a particular religious/spiritual community or not, we welcome you! This website is designed to give you a deeper sense of the kind of work that we do at Yale as well as to promote religious literacy for the greater purpose of fostering understanding and appreciation of global religious and spiritual traditions. name: Yale University Dramatic Association, Inc.
description: The Yale Dramat is dedicated to producing inclusive and diverse theater - that is accessible to the Yale - New Haven community and intends to impact these communities, through conversation, performance, and education, - as well as upholding the Dramat's long tradition of fine theater.

name: Yale University Graduate Outing Club
description: The YGOC is a forum for planning day trips in and around Connecticut and for meeting others from across the Yale graduate and professional schools. Every couple of weeks, we send out a list of upcoming trips. Anyone can join, no experience (nor car) necessary. That's the whole system. The trips happen because people (possibly even you!) propose them and others volunteer to drive. The more members, the more trips and opportunities to join.

name: Yale University Undergraduate Women in Economics
description: The goal of the Women in Economics organization is to support women pursuing a degree in economics and to introduce more undergraduate women to the field. To do so, we showcase the wide variety of fields within economics; bring together undergraduates, graduate students, and faculty; and host events that celebrate the achievements of the women in the discipline. We are dedicated to building a broad, supportive, and engaged community within the department.

name: Yale Venture Club for Students and Scholars
description: 1. Unite entrepreneurs, industry experts, VC/PE investors, and all others with a genuine interest in the venture field among the Yale community. 3. description: We are inspired to perform plays with bilingual (Mandarin and English) versions, so as to facilitate cultural conversations and build a bridge between the theater work based in these two language mediums. We also see great value in forming such a cultural club in light of the spike in anti-AAPI sentiments since the start of the pandemic. We are naming the club "Vermilion Theater" as the vermilion bird (a phoenix-like being) is a symbol of tenacity and resilience in Chinese mythology. name: Yale Veterans and Military in Medicine
description: We strive to provide a space for community building among Service Members and veterans at YSM, to foster mentorship from faculty with military background, and to connect YSM students with military and veteran groups throughout the greater Yale University community.

name: Yale Veterans Network
description: The YVN's vision is to make Yale the employer of choice for veterans, reservists, and guardsmen while creating a community to support and encourage the career development and growth of all its members.

name: Yale Vexillology Society - An Undergraduate Organization
description: The Yale Vexillology Society aims to provide unique opportunities to students interested in the blossoming field of flags. Since 2015, over 300 American cities and 4 countries have undergone lengthy processes to alter the banners that represent their otherwise intangible cultural heritage, and students at universities across the country have banded together to study and participate in these emergent trends. name: Yale Visual Arts Collective - an Undergraduate Organization
description: Our mission is to create a dialogue between student artists at Yale, in an environment that addresses both the established and the experimental, while being accessible to students that range from beginners to advanced art students. In the process, we hope to enhance people's lives through fun, creativity, and self-expression, while advancing artistic excellence and innovation for the benefit of individuals and the greater New Haven community.

name: Yale Vot-ER
description: Healthy Communities Powered By A Healthy Democracy: Vot-ER is a nonpartisan organization working to bring voter registration into the health system

name: Yale Well
description: To foster an environment that supports and advances students' wellness, in all its dimensions, through innovative programs, opportunities for self-discovery and growth, and the cultivation of a compassionate campus culture.

name: Yale West Campus
description: The Office of Public Affairs & Communications (OPAC) maintains Yale University's public events calendar. When an event created in Yale Connect 'co-hosts' with the Yale Public Events Calendar group, the event will be automatically submitted to OPAC for review and approval for display in the University's public calendar.

name: Yale Women in Architecture
description: Yale Women in Architecture - Student Chapter is committed to promoting equity in architecture, design, and related fields. Through mentorship, advocacy, and diverse programming, we strive to foster an inclusive, collaborative, and empowering environment while offering opportunities for professional growth, leadership, and discourse for students at the YSoA. YWA Student Chapter welcomes everyone who supports our mission to take part in improving the practice of architecture worldwide.

name: Yale Women's Athletic Council: An Undergraduate Empowerment Group
description: This council aims to unite and empower the female athletic community at Yale through fostering positive conversation and creating a community of acceptance. Our goal is to promote the physical and emotional well-being of female athletes on campus through various initiatives, speakers, and events.

name: Yale Young Global Scholars
description: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS) is one of the most globally diverse, two-week academic summer programs in the world. Serving over 2,000 students from 150+ countries and all 50 U.S. states, YYGS distributes over $3 Million USD in need-based financial aid to both domestic and international students.

name: YaleBleeds – A Student Movement
description: YaleBleeds's mission is to destigmatize menstruation and work towards menstrual equity at Yale, in New Haven, in Connecticut, in the United States, and beyond. This includes advocacy, education, and service/volunteering work. Advocacy work includes working to increase access to free menstrual products — both disposable and reusable — on campus or wider legislative work in communities outside Yale (such as New Haven Public Schools, Connecticut, and more). Education includes hosting workshops on period poverty and menstrual equity, sustainable menstrual products, the intersection of LGBTQ+ exper

name: Yaledancers - An Undergraduate Organization
description: Yaledancers is Yale's oldest premier dance company. Since 1973, YD has provided Yale student dancers with access to high-caliber training and performance opportunities. Yaledancers stages semesterly company shows and performs at other University functions, all of which showcase original student choreography. In addition to rehearsals for these shows, YD meets twice weekly for classes, taught by both company members and industry professionals. The company practices and performs a wide variety of dance styles, including classical and contemporary ballet, jazz, contemporary, tap, musical theatre,

name: Yalies for Pakistan
description: Yalies for Pakistan seeks to showcase Pakistan to the broader Yale community. We intend to provide students with a community, a home away from home, and a platform to discuss Pakistani culture, politics, and current affairs.

name: Yalies Fronterizos - An Undergraduate Student Organization
description: Yalies Fronterizos exists to celebrate and support students with connections to, or interest in, the US-México borderlands. Our goal is to cultivate a community that embraces and respects the unique cultural heritage through a variety of social and cultural events. We facilitate bilingual dialogue and connection, enriching the Yale community with the vibrant diversity of borderland experiences.

name: YDS Academic Affairs
description: At Yale Divinity School, students pursue varied vocations through a variety of degree programs, which draw on a rich array of curricular offerings across the theological disciplines. The Office of Academic Affairs is responsible for academic and curricular programs and works collaboratively with the Dean, the faculty, teaching fellows, and students to address academic concerns and craft appropriate policies and procedures for the School. The Registrar's Office is part of the Office of Academic Affairs and handles academic needs of students. The Office of Vocation and Leadership, also under the

name: YDS Anglican Student Fellowship
description: YDS Anglican Fellowship is a community-building organization for all those Yale Divinity School students interested in Episcopal (and global Anglican Communion) fellowship, conversation, and community-building. We are an organization welcoming of, but not limited to, students who also participate in Berkeley activities!

name: YDS Asian Students Association
description: Asian Students Association (ASA) provides a place for fellowship in the sharing of an ethnic bond and common faith. ASA is an inclusive space and community for students of Asian heritage, whether domestic or international students, along with fellow YDS students that are interested in advocacy of Asian/American issues. Frequent meetings roundtable discussions on current Asian/American theological issues, academic forums for the advancement of Asian-American theology, and fellowship gatherings.

name: YDS Commencement
description: The official Yale Connect page for the Yale Divinity School Commencement. Events, information, and communications for all graduating students.

name: YDS Communications Office
description: The Communications Office works in concert with our colleagues and constituents on the Quad, at the university, and across the greater YDS community to promote understanding of the Divinity School and our mission and values, with particular emphasis on attracting students and cultivating affinity with our alumni and other supporters. Our primary areas of responsibility are: publications and marketing, media relations, social media, and the YDS website.

name: YDS DivFarm Student Group
description: The DivFarm serves as a space to foster growth food for students and local community, spiritual growth, and growth of community. We provide space for students and with local community members to plant and maintain their plots. It does this through personal plots for local individuals, community programming events, sustainability education, worship and mindfulness events, and as a managed space that people are free to visit and enjoy. We advocate for sustainability, environmental justice, food sovereignty, and lifelong experiential learning.

name: YDS International Students Association
description: The International Students Association (ISA) at Yale Divinity School exists to support and advocate for the interests of international students. Our mission is to provide a platform for cultural exchange, fellowship, and mutual support among students from diverse backgrounds. ISA facilitates events, activities, and programs that promote cross-cultural understanding and enrich the YDS community through the sharing of global perspectives. Additionally, ISA serves as a resource for guidance and information on the unique challenges international students face., helping them to thrive academically,

name: YDS Knitting & Crochet Group
description: The YDS Knitting Club is a fun and friendly group for all crochet and knitting enthusiasts at Yale Divinity School. Whether you're a pro or just starting out, join us to knit, crochet, learn, chat, and unwind. Come make new friends and create beautiful, cozy items together!

name: YDS Office of Faculty Affairs
description: The Office of Faculty Affairs provides a variety of resources to support YDS faculty members in all aspects of their professional lives as scholars, teachers, and citizens of the university. This includes information related to faculty development, research support, faculty searches, promotion and tenure policies and procedures, teaching resources, and general information. The Office of Faculty Affairs can also direct faculty to relevant resources within the University and beyond.

name: YDS Office of Student Affairs (OSA)
description: The Yale Divinity School Office of Student Affairs seeks to enrich all aspects of student life at YDS. The Office of Student Affairs exists to: - Advocate for Yale Divinity School Students - Support the Community Life Committee (CLC) - Empower Yale Divinity School Student Government (YDSG) - Nurture YDS Student Group leadership In addition, the YDS Office of Student Affairs assists students with personal matters, academic concerns, and resources for students with disabilities. name: YDS Paracleats Soccer Team
description: The Yale Divinity School Paracleats: A Student Soccer Club are an intramural soccer in the Yale University Intramural League. People of all enthusiasm and abilities are welcome! It does not matter if you played in college or have never kicked a soccer ball, we can find a place for you and want you on the team.

name: YDS SAGES
description: This group will provide peer support and advocacy for those entering divinity school having already spent considerable time in prior occupations, professional careers, parenting or other family support, or other life experiences.

name: YDS Student Musicians Collective
description: As a club, we aim: (1) to gather and discuss about music during weekly lunches, and (2) to host music performance opportunities (lunchtime salon concerts) to share our musical talents with the YDS community at large. We distinguish ourselves from performing in liturgical contexts, such as one would find in Marquand.

name: YDS Student Org Leaders
description: The YDS Student Leaders' Handbook is the central resource for all Student Leaders of Clubs and Representatives in the YDS Student Government. The website is the official handbook of the YDS student org community, and events are regularly posted for training and development of our student leaders. Student leaders needing access should email Kit.Heeley@yale.edu for access.

name: YDS Women's Center
description: The YDSWC is a community welcoming of all people and focuses specifically on issues surrounding those who identify in various ways with womanhood. The YDSWC commits to creating a brave space on campus where women and allies can gather to share resources, knowledge, and stories, and advocate for women's rights.

name: Yeater
description: The mission of Yeater is to explore and document the diverse culinary scene at Yale and New Haven, offering insights, reviews, and recommendations from a student perspective. This club aims to enhance the appreciation of food culture among Yale students and foster a community of food enthusiasts and writers.

name: YEP! at Yale - an Undergraduate Organization
description: YEP! is an entirely free entrepreneurship program for local high school students in New Haven. By inviting local students onto campus to participate in an entrepreneurship incubator, YEP! hopes to develop the next generation of entrepreneurs and strengthen town-gown relations.

name: YHack Organization
description: YHack is Yale's largest annual student-run hackathon and aims to foster a diverse, innovative and collaborative environment in which students are equipped to use computer science fundamentals to devise real-world solutions. We hope to provide students with opportunities to develop novel approaches to problems and gain access to a passionate network of passionate individuals.

name: YLS Career Development Office
description: Yale Law School's Career Development Office (CDO) provides a variety of resources to assist you in making informed career decisions. A good starting point is the career pathways section of this site where you can learn about the variety of employment opportunities available. Use the toolkit for student job seekers to guide you through the self-assessment, employer research, application and interview processes. name: YLS Coker Fellows
description: Those students who will be third-year students (or the equivalent) in the Fall are eligible to apply for positions as Coker Fellows, teaching assistants that work with the first-year small groups.

name: YLW+
description: YLW+ works to advance the status of women and underrepresented gender identities at YLS and in the legal profession at large. To realize this mission, we create programming, resources, and mentorship opportunities to bolster our members' pursuit of their professional and personal goals. YLW+ is a non-partisan organization committed to building a supportive community at YLS and beyond.

name: Young Associates from Newly Independent States (YANIS)
description: The purpose of YANIS shall be to promote and develop the community of Yale students and postdocs from the Newly Independent States (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan) by the means of language and cultural accommodations. YANIS is also open to all Russian-speaking students and those interested in learning Russian.

name: Young Israel House at Yale
description: Young Israel House at Yale (YIHY) represents the Orthodox Jewish community at Yale, catering to the needs of observant Jews on campus. As a group, we arrange minyan services, Jewish learning initiatives, and other activities and events for the Yale Jewish community at large.

name: Youth in Motion
description: We are a group of dancers, teachers, and people who love working with young people and come together twice a week to dance, laugh, and learn with our wonderful students. Our mission is to promote creative self-expression and mutual understanding through movement and creativity.

name: YSE Business and the Environment Learning Community
description: Students who engage with this LC join a dynamic circle of scholars and practitioners who are thinking about the many opportunities and challenges for businesses in developing more sustainable approaches to meeting human needs.

name: YSE Chess Club
description: Our mission is to create a space where people can play chess, build their skills, or learn the game for the first time. We hope to strengthen the YSE community through friendly competition. We also aim to attract beginners, so I will host simple lessons on the fundamentals of chess. We want people of all skill levels to come to our meetings and learn something new.

name: YSE Climate Change Science and Solutions Learning Community
description: Businesses, ecosystems, industries, societies, and political systems are all vulnerable to climate change. This LC focuses on the science of climate change and on investigating innovative, interdisciplinary ways to address it.

name: YSE Commencement
description: The official Yale Connect page for the Yale School of the Environment Commencement. Events, information, and communications for all graduating students.

name: YSE Ecosystem Management and Conservation Learning Community
description: Students engaged with this LC build a knowledge base and develop skills they can use to help steward and conserve ecosystems, ensuring that human and nonhuman species can coexist across landscapes.

name: YSE Energy and the Environment Learning Community
description: Students engaging with this LC examine issues related to energy systems and technologies, policies, and economics — helping them to build a knowledge base they can use to assess the problems posed by both traditional and emerging alternative energy sources.

name: YSE Environmental Policy Analysis Learning Community
description: This LC helps students gain a deeper understanding of the foundations and methods of policy analysis, including how to evaluate their strengths and weaknesses and how to apply these frameworks to a broad range of environmental and resource management issues.

description: Yale: The FGLI Community Initiative partners with students who are first in their families to attend college, lower-income, and/or DACA/Undocumented. The FGLI Community Initiative works with these students to foster identity development, navigate campus resources, and build community. Through campus-wide partnerships and advocacy, the FGLI Community Initiative strives to build an inclusive Yale community that is welcoming, supportive, and accessible for all students.

name: YSE Forestry Learning Community
description: Building on over a century of leadership in forestry and land conservation, this LC helps students gain the knowledge base they need to work collaboratively across environmental disciplines to manage forests in a way that respects the land and one another.

name: YSE Industrial Ecology and Green Chemistry Learning Community
description: Industrial ecology and green design are key to addressing many of the sustainability challenges posed by ever-increasing industrial production.In this LC, students study the energy and materials used in industry, and develop strategic approaches to the design, use, and re-use of materials.

description: Career success and career development programming for YSE International Students.

description: This LC helps students develop the skills they need to thoughtfully critique and improve the relationship between people and the planet, with a focus on deep-seated, systemic challenges. Emphasis is placed on the interplay among the environment, systemic social issues, and the emerging environmental justice movement.

name: YSE Professional Communication Center
description: Our mission is to enhance YSE students' communication skills and confidence in interviewing, writing, and presenting. From foundational skill building to high stakes events, we help students rise to the challenge of opportunities at YSE and beyond.

name: YSE Semester of Service (SIG)
description: To build on the culture of service within YSE that 1) strengthens relationships between YSE students and New Haven, 2) builds on New Haven communities’ strengths, and 3) gives students an opportunity to learn from a wide range of New Haven organisations

name: YSE Urban Learning Community
description: We examine the impacts of an 'urbanized' world, from effects on resources and biodiversity to public health and climate change.

description: The mission of the YSM Wellness Committee is to foster an environment of healthy and sustainable living among students at YSM.

name: YSM Craft Collective
description: The YSM Craft Collective provides opportunities for medical students to unwind, express their creativity, and build community — both with each other and with the patients we serve. We host monthly craft circle socials and lead art activity groups with patients at Yale New Haven Hospital and the Connecticut Mental Health Center. All forms of arts and crafts and all experience levels are welcome!

name: YSM First Generation, Low Income Affinity Group
YSM Habitat for Humanity
description: YSM Habitat for Humanity aims to connect with local community beyond Yale by volunteering with the New Haven chapter of Habitat for Humanity which supports families in need by providing and building affordable housing.

description: Fostering collaboration, innovation, and professional growth by uniting Yale’s Immunobiology community to exchange ideas, advance research, and build connections shaping the future of the field.

name: YSM Office of Alumni Affairs
description: Whether facilitating volunteer efforts, an event or philanthropic support, the office is dedicated to serving and promoting the interests of current and future alumni, as they pursue their role as leaders in medicine, healthcare delivery, and the biomedical sciences. The office works closely with the alumni leadership of the Association of Yale Alumni in Medicine (AYAM), the AYAM committees, and other alumni organizations to identify, create and implement alumni programs that serve and enhance the School's education, research and clinical missions.

name: YSM Office of Student Affairs
description: The Office of Student Affairs at the Yale School of Medicine helps students navigate their medical education from Orientation to Graduation. We provide academic advising, support student groups and wellness, promote student life and community building activities, and act as the primary resource for students who are seeking to find balance in their medical school experience.

name: YSM Physician Associate Program
description: The mission of the Yale School of Medicine Physician Associate Program is to educate outstanding clinicians and to foster leaders who will serve their communities and advance quality healthcare.

name: YSM Social Committee (MD, MD-PhD)
description: The YSM Social Committee is responsible for planning social events open to the entire student body. We plan events from ClubMeds/PubMeds, to smaller study breaks.

name: YSoA Makes
description: YSoA Makes is a student-led group that creates opportunities for hands-on fabrication. Through specialized workshops, skill-sharing, and collaborative build projects, we aim to empower a community of makers.

name: YSoA Yoga (YSoAY)
description: Bring the benrfits of yoga to the YSoA students, faculty, and staff.

name: YSPH Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging
description: Across the YSPH community, the dean, faculty, staff and the alumni have adopted mentorship, recruitment, retention and professional development practices to help meet our goal of having an outstanding and diverse School of Public Health—a place that better reflects the local, national and international communities we study. The Diversity Ambassadors at YSPH exist to serve as advocates for students and liaisons between the student affinity groups and the larger Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging Committee (DEIB).

name: YSPH Student Veterans Group
parent: Yale School of Public Health Student Organizations
description: The YSPH Student Veteran Group connects military veterans and their families of all services and nationalities to foster a space where veterans can share experiences, build connections, and support one another in their personal and academic journeys. Our mission is to support current veteran students, assist prospective veteran students, and share experiences gained from the military with the greater YSPH community, fostering understanding and unity.
